injuries.detail: Love will miss a fourth consecutive game Sunday but will then be eligible to come off injured reserve ahead of Week 13 against the Eagles. LaFleur previously said Love will be reevaluated Monday once eligible to return, and the coach added Friday that he expects to know more Wednesday once the Cardinals return to practice. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight are still the leading in-house backfield options in the meantime.

Johnson, who completed 18 of 31 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown in a 34-7 loss to Kansas City in Week 11, is thus set to make his second straight start for the Cardinals. With no teams on bye this week, Johnson's Week 12 fantasy utility is limited to Superflex formats and to fantasy managers scrambling for a short-term injury replacement at the QB position.

Beck has yet to resume practicing and will miss a second consecutive game Sunday due to back spasms, paving the way for Josh Johnson to start against Washington. LaFleur added that a Week 13 return against the Eagles is in play for Beck, who made his first regular-season NFL start in a 34-6 Week 10 loss to the Rams. Beck's practice participation level leading up to that game will provide an indication regarding his potential availability, and LaFleur added that the team will know more about Beck's status "early in the week," per Weinfuss.

Slovis had been waived by the Ravens earlier in the week, and while the team hoped to bring him back, the equally quarterback-embattled Cardinals swooped in and claimed him. With that, Slovis returns to the team he played for in 2025.

Gibbens was able to lead the team in takedowns in Week 11, recording double-digit tackles for the second time in four weeks. The linebacker has now compiled 76 total tackles (33 solo), including 0.5 sacks, while also notching a pass defensed over 11 contests so far this season.

Baker was able to register at least six stops for the fourth week in a row and seventh time overall this year. The safety is about as steady as they come, compiling 74 total tackles (36 solo), including a career-high 3.5 sacks, while also adding an interception and a forced fumble over 11 contests so far during the 2026 season.

Wilson was able to register at least eight stops for the second straight week and fifth time overall this season. The linebacker has now compiled 80 total tackles (35 solo), two passes defensed and a forced fumble over 11 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

Duvernay played two offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver took a step back after drawing three targets in Week 10, as both Simi Fehoko and Harrison Wallace were clearly ahead of him Sunday.

The 22-year-old wide receiver played just two offensive snaps, the same amount as Devin Duvernay, as the duo played behind all three of Simi Fehoko (52 snaps), Harrison Wallace (36) and Zay Jones (32) in the Cardinals' injury-ravaged wideout depth chart. Virgil has three catches for 54 yards on 11 targets across seven games this season and therefore doesn't possess any fantasy relevance at the moment.

The Cardinals offense struggled Sunday with Josh Johnson as the starter in the absence of Carson Beck (back). Of Johnson's 31 pass attempts, 26 of them were split between Trey McBride (14), Harrison Wallace (seven) and Simi Fehoko (five), leaving very little for Higgins and the other Cardinals pass catchers. Higgins has only one catch over his last two outings and a 19-166-1 line on 21 targets through 11 regular-season games.

The wideout led his position group by playing 52 of 56 offensive snaps, and he ran a team-high 34 routes on Josh Johnson's 37 dropbacks. It didn't translate to much production outside of the short touchdown, as Fehoko has consistently shown he can't win enough as an NFL receiver. He's been thrust into heavy snaps due to a litany of injuries in Arizona. Fehoko can mostly be ignored in fantasy until he shows something more in the box score.

Jones' 32 snaps on offense during Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs were ahead of both Devin Duvernay and Reggie Virgil (two each) and behind Simi Fehoko (52) and Harrison Wallace (36). Jones finished the game with a one-yard carry and a 17-yard catch on two targets, and that reception ended up being the second-longest offensive play for the Cardinals. Given his usage in Week 11, Jones stands a good chance of being brought up for Week 12 against the Commanders on Nov. 29, although his next elevation from the practice squad is the last one he is eligible for this season.

Wallace began the season on the Cardinals' practice squad and didn't play in his first NFL game until Week 9 versus Seattle. After logging a total of seven offensive snaps and one catch across his first two contests, the rookie paced Arizona wideouts in targets, receptions and receiving yards. Wallace also ranked second among the wideout corps with 36 offensive snaps, so it appears there was a conscious effort to involve him in the team's passing game. The Cardinals' wide-receiver room has lacked a reliable option since Michael Wilson went down with a season-ending neck injury, so the door is wide open for Wallace to claim a prominent role with continued production.

Playing with their third- and fourth-string quarterbacks, the Cardinals have mustered a total of 13 points over their last two games. Ryland has minimal fantasy appeal in an offense struggling to simply move the ball. On the season, he's 22-for-24 on field-goal tries and 17-for-18 on PATs across 11 games.

Since coming out of nowhere to post two receiving touchdowns in his Cardinals debut back in Week 5 against the Lions, Quitoriano has fallen out of the mix for playing time on offense. After the two-score effort, Quitoriano logged double-digit snaps on offense in four straight contests, but he drew just one target over that stretch. In the subsequent two games, Quitoriano has played just three total snaps on offense while Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins and Hunter Long have been prioritized ahead of him at tight end.

Although he split the backfield workload nearly equally with Tyler Allgeier, Knight was the more productive RB, although he still failed to reach 50 rushing yards for a fourth straight game. The 25-year-old running back gets a more favorable matchup in Week 12 against the Commanders, but Knight and Allgeier could face additional competition for touches if Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is cleared to return.

Game script fairly quickly put the Cardinals' running game in mothballs, and Allgeier wound up splitting the backfield workload nearly equally with Bam Knight, who picked up 45 scrimmage yards on eight touches. Allgeier has gone three straight games without reaching 50 rushing yards or getting into the end zone, but those games were also against very tough opponents (the Seahawks in Week 9 and the Rams in Week 10). The fifth-year RB could find a little more running room in Week 12 against the Commanders, but Jeremiyah Love (ankle) might also be ready to rejoin the lineup by then.

Working with his fourth quarterback of the season in Josh Johnson, McBride dominated the 40-year-old's attention, as no other Cardinal got more than seven targets or hauled in more than four passes. The star tight end wasn't able to do much with the volume, however, as his longest gain went for a mere nine yards. Carson Beck (back) could be back under center in Week 12 against the Commanders, but that might not improve McBride's outlook, as he saw only five targets in Week 10 during the rookie QB's first NFL start.

Simon is being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's contest. His absence gives the Cardinals less depth at linebacker behind Jack Gibbens, Mack Wilson and Zaven Collins.

Branch will join Jahan Dotson (hamstring) on the sidelines in Week 12. Drake London, Olamide Zaccheaus, Beaux Collins and Chris Blair are Atlanta's available options at wide receiver, while Zaccheaus and Khalil Herbert are the top candidates to handle punt returns and kickoff returns in Branch's absence. Branch's next opportunity to suit up will be Dec. 6 against Detroit.

Coming off Atlanta's Week 11 bye, Dotson was a listed DNP on all three of the team's Week 12 practice reports due to a hamstring injury, which will force his first missed game of the season. With fellow WR Zachariah Branch (hamstring) also out Sunday, the Falcons' depth at the position is a bit thin behind Drake London and Olamide Zaccheaus, as Beaux Collins and Chris Blair are the other options on the active roster. As a result, Dylan Drummond, Antwane Wells and Vinny Anthony will be candidates to be brought up from the practice squad.

Pearce was listed as a limited participant Wednesday but was able to practice without limitations one day later. As such, he should be good to go for Sunday's matchup in Minnesota.

Daniels has been dealing with an Achilles issue since late October, but is hasn't yet caused him to miss any games. With that in mind, unless he's suffered a setback, Daniels seems likely to suit up Sunday in Minnesota. He's had a solid rookie season, tallying 69 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, two defensed passes (including an interception) and one fumble recovery through 10 contests.

Deablo aggravated a forearm injury against the Bengals in Week 9, which prevented him from playing against the Chiefs in Week 10. He's had additional time to recover courtesy of the bye, and given his absence from Wednesday's injury report, Deablo is on track to play against the Vikings on Sunday.

Zaccheaus recorded a season-high 17 receiving yards during the loss while playing 29 snaps on offense and 14 on special teams. The 29-year-old has hauled in eight passes for 43 yards in addition to amassing 231 kick-return yards and 81 punt-return yards across nine games this season.

Herbert was targeted three times for the second straight game in Week 10, but he continued to make a bigger impact on special teams. His first kickoff return of the day went for 39 yards to Atlanta's 45-yard line, but the offense promptly went three and out. He'll be hoping to keep up the momentum as a returner following the Falcons' bye in Week 11.

Moody was signed by the Falcons off the Ravens' practice squad Tuesday, and he was able to put together a perfect debut with the team in Week 10. The kicker converted a 28-yard field-goal try in the second quarter before later adding a 38-yard make in the fourth. With Atlanta's bye week in Week 11, Moody's next chance to build on Sunday's performance will come in Week 12 against the Vikings.

Hooper was on the field for just 11 of the Falcons' 72 offensive snaps, with his 15 percent share placing him comfortably behind Kyle Pitts (76 percent) and Charlie Woerner (44 percent) among Atlanta tight ends. The 32-year-old Hooper hasn't played more than half of the snaps in any of Atlanta's first 10 games and has turned in a 10-84-1 receiving line on 12 targets, a level of production that keeps him well off the fantasy radar.

London was checked for a possible concussion in the fourth quarter of Week 10 action, but the result of the evaluation wasn't reported before the game concluded. Prior to his exit Sunday, he posted his third 100-yard game (109, to be exact) of the campaign on six catches and a season-high 12 targets. London will continue to operate as the Falcons' No. 1 WR after a Week 11 bye in the team's next game Sunday, Nov. 29, at Minnesota.

Penix struggled while the game was still in question, but he did manage to pad his stats some down the stretch as the Falcons unsuccessfully tried to overcome their deficit. Penix connected with eight different targets overall on the afternoon, and he ultimately finished with a season high in passing yards. Penix has now tossed six interceptions in the last three games, however, and he'll look to regroup during the Week 11 bye before tackling a difficult matchup against the Vikings on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

The veteran tight end had a slow start to the day before coming on when the Falcons went especially pass-heavy in the second half. Pitts' fumble, his first of the season, came with just over four minutes remaining in the game after the contest was out of reach, and his catch total was his highest since Week 7. Pitts remains a key complementary option in an Atlanta passing attack that's scuffled of late, and he'll look to bounce back after the Falcons emerge from a Week 11 bye with a Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

The Falcons were down 14-3 by halftime and 21-3 doing into the final period, so Robinson's opportunities progressively dwindled due to game script. However, the star running back still averaged a solid 4.4 yards per carry and recorded his sixth rushing touchdown of the season on a three-yard run in the fourth quarter. Robinson has at least four receptions in three of the last four games, and he'll now have a Week 11 bye to rest up before a tough Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Henry has cleared concussion protocol after practicing without limitations Thursday and Friday. He'll try to help the Ravens snap a six-game losing streak Sunday against the Texans. Running room could be hard to come by against a stout Houston front that's allowing fewer than 100 rushing yards per game, though Henry has overcome more than his fair share of daunting matchups over the years.

Green's practice reps were limited Wednesday due to a knee injury, but his full session Thursday puts him on track to play against the Texans on Sunday. The second-year edge rusher has accumulated 32 tackles (20 solo), including 7.5 sacks, across 11 regular-season games.

Hawkins was held out of Wednesday's practice due to a lingering knee injury, which has prevented him from playing in each of the Ravens' last five games. However, a full session Friday could be enough for Hawkins to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans.

Bateman was limited in Wednesday's session due to a groin injury, but his full practice Thursday puts the sixth-year wide receiver on track to play against the Texans on Sunday. He hauled in his second touchdown of the year in a Week 11 loss to the Panthers and is up to a 25-403-2 receiving line on 42 targets through 11 regular-season games.

Flowers was limited at practice Wednesday, but the wide receiver's quick return to all activity one day later clears the way for him to suit up Sunday against the Texans. In his last outing, Flowers (who has recorded a fantasy-friendly 57-785-3 line on 82 targets through 10 games), was on the field for 88 percent of his team's snaps on offense in a 35-33 loss to the Panthers in Week 11 en route to catching eight of his game-high 11 targets for 97 yards.

Humphrey was a healthy inactive for Week 11 against the Panthers after making negative comments about the city of Baltimore on his podcast. It's unclear whether he'll play against the Texans on Sunday, with head coach Jesse Minter telling reporters Monday that the Ravens will make a decision about Humphrey's availability by the end of the week.

Jones got his first sack of the season in Week 11, and his eight total tackles were a career high. He should retain a big role on the interior of the Ravens' defensive line in a Week 12 tilt at Houston, and he'll be looking to keep up the momentum in that contest.

Simpson was able to secure his first double-digit tackle performance of the year, leading the team in takedowns in Week 11. The linebacker has now compiled a career-high 75 total tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also intercepting a pass and recovering a fumble over 11 contests so far during the 2026 season.

Hamilton was able to notch at least eight takedowns for the second week in a row and fourth time this season. The safety has now registered 78 total tackles (55 solo) and five passes defensed, including an interception, while also forcing a fumble over 11 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

Smith has at least eight tackles in 10 of 11 games this season but has just two games with double-digit tackles. On the season, the veteran linebacker has piled up 91 tackles (40 solo), including 2.0 sacks, four pass breakups, including an interception, and two forced fumbles on 94 percent of the defensive snaps.

Cuevas continues to draw targets at an impressive clip, tallying three for his second straight game despite only being on the field for 14 of the Ravens' 61 offensive snaps in Week 11. Barring an injury to starter Mark Andrews or rookie fourth-rounder Matt Hibner, though, his role isn't big enough to warrant fantasy consideration in most formats. Baltimore will take on the Texans in Week 12.

Lane failed to reel in a pass for the second time in three weeks, and both times the ball was thrown his way Sunday, the play was negated by a defensive penalty, resulting in no targets for the rookie. He was on the field for 33 offensive snaps, ranking third at wide receiver for Baltimore behind Rashod Bateman (59) and Zay Flowers (57). Lane's next chance to get back on track will come in Week 12 against the Texans.

The wide receiver filled a returner role for the first time this season and did well. Walker has seen just 10 targets on offense in 2026, so he's not much of a factor in fantasy leagues at the moment, but he could garner more opportunities on special teams following Sunday's success.

Patterson was able to convert his only field-goal try in Week 11, nailing a chip-shot 28-yard attempt in the first quarter. He's now combined to go 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts while making all six of his PATs over two contests as the starting kicker for Baltimore, and he likely will remain in that role for Week 12 with Tyler Loop (groin) sidelined for at least one more contest.

Hibner logged 35 of 65 snaps on offense, with his 54 percent share ranking second to only Mark Andrews (62 percent) among Ravens tight ends. The rookie fourth-round pick out of SMU's playing time has held steady between 30 and 60 percent of snaps over his 10 appearances, with Hibner drawing no more than two targets in any of those contests.

While the veteran tight end showed some instant chemistry with new quarterback Jacoby Brissett last week, Andrews saw his target volume crater in their second game together, as rookie depth TEs Josh Cuevas and Matthew Hibner saw similar usage as pass catchers. Andrews has failed to reach 25 receiving yards in five of his last six games and hasn't scored a TD in seven straight contests, making him a very risky fantasy option in Week 12 against the Texans.

Derrick Henry had a strong performance as well but was knocked out of the game in the fourth quarter and got checked for a concussion. Hill was heavily involved in the offense prior to that, however, scoring from 19 yards out in the late in the second quarter. He almost had a second TD earlier in the quarter, but Hill had the ball punched loose at the one-yard line after a 36-yard scamper and saw it bounce out of the end zone for a turnover and a touchback. Henry cleared the concussion protocol after the game and figures to be active in the Week 12 against the Texans, but Hill's usage appears to be on the upswing as the Ravens' No. 2 back.

It was another decent showing for the veteran quarterback, and his first TD pass in two games as a Raven came on a trick that involved a direct snap to Derrick Henry, who flipped it Brissett for a 52-yard strike to Rashod Bateman. Brissett has also kept Zay Flowers relevant, feeding the wideout 18 targets for a 14-171-0 line. Baltimore's passing attack will try to keep improving in Week 12 against the Texans.

Coleman's involvement was minimal with DJ Moore healthy, as has been the case throughout the season. Josh Allen threw for just 81 yards Thursday, so none of Buffalo's receivers were particularly effective, but it would likely take another injury to Moore for Coleman -- who logged a 49 percent snap share in the contest -- to return to relevance in fantasy. Coleman hasn't exceeded 17 yards in a game or scored since Week 6. Up next for Coleman and the Bills is a Week 13 trip to New England.

Knox finished without a catch while Dalton Kincaid caught both of his targets in the latter's return from a one-game absence due to thumb and ankle injuries. Josh Allen threw for just 81 yards in difficult weather conditions, but Knox hasn't contributed much as a pass catcher even when Allen has been slinging the ball effectively. Heading into a Week 13 trip to New England, Knox has caught 16 of 24 targets for 117 yards and one TD through 11 appearances.

Shakir's reception and yardage totals led the Bills on a night when Josh Allen threw for just 81 yards with a pair of picks. The veteran slot receiver was coming off a Week 11 showing against the Dolphins in which he accrued a season-high 101 receiving yards, and Thursday's downturn was largely explainable by Allen's struggles and less-than-ideal weather conditions. Shakir should remain a key target for Allen during a Week 13 road matchup Sunday, Dec. 6 with a Patriots squad that the wideout posted a 7-82-0 line against back in Week 4.

Moore's production, like that of the rest of his fellow skill-position players, was very modest on a night when Josh Allen threw for only 81 yards and a pair of interceptions. The talented wideout's catch and yardage totals were both his third-lowest tallies of the season, but Moore is still averaging a formidable 14.6 yards per reception heading into a Week 13 road matchup against the Patriots on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Making his return from a one-game absence due to thumb and ankle injuries, Kincaid's numbers weren't quite as poor within the context of a night where Josh Allen threw for only 81 yards and completed less than 50.0 percent of his passes. Kincaid tied for runner-up slotting on the Bills in receptions, and he was third in receiving yards as well. Kincaid now has multiple catches in five straight games heading into a Week 13 road divisional matchup against the Patriots on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Allen's abysmal numbers tell the tale of how difficult a night it was for the star signal-caller under less-than-ideal weather conditions and while facing a talented veteran defense. Allen's passing yardage total was a season low, and the two-interception  tally was his second straight. Allen also took a pair of sacks and completed a season-worst 47.6 percent of his passes, but he helped bring Buffalo back from a 10-7 fourth-quarter deficit. Allen's lackluster showing aside, he'll remain an elite option in all formats for a Week 13 road divisional clash against the Patriots on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Cook logged a season high in rush attempts while eclipsing the century mark for the third time in the last four games. Cook's longest gain went for only 10 yards, so he worked hard for everything he got against a tough Chiefs front. Cook added his 11th rushing touchdown of the season on a five-yard run early in the second quarter, and he'll have some extra recovery time before he takes aim at the Patriots defense in a Week 13 road matchup on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Sanders has been officially cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a shoulder injury, and his presence means DeWayne Carter will revert to a rotational role at defensive end for Thanksgiving Day. Sanders has 11 tackles (five solo) through five regular-season games.

Williams didn't play against the Dolphins in Week 11 due to a calf injury, but the fourth-year pro has been cleared by medical staff to play Thursday. He has accumulated 61 tackles (27 solo), including 1.0 sacks, four pass defenses (including two interceptions) and one fumble recovery across nine regular-season games.

Benford will end up missing a second consecutive game due to a groin injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Jets. Maxwell Hairston should see a bump in defensive snaps at outside cornerback in the absence of Benford, whose next chance to play is Week 13 against the Patriots on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Rousseau was limited in Monday's session while managing a back injury, but his full participation Tuesday indicates that the sixth-year edge rusher will be available against the Chiefs on Thanksgiving Day. Rousseau logged two sacks against the Dolphins on Sunday, and his 10.0 sacks through 10 regular-season games are second-most in the NFL behind Will Anderson (11.5).

Hooker has now played in two games for the Bills, logging 100 percent of the team's defensive reps in Week 11 and 98 percent in Week 12. The strong safety has made for a good pairing with Cole Bishop, and the duo has helped the Bills' defense extend its streak of not allowing a touchdown to 15 straight quarters of play.

Bernard had his lowest output of the season in Sunday's contest. The linebacker played 28 defensive snaps, equating to 62 percent of the team's defensive plays. The defensive captain was likely pulled early to rest for Thursday night's primetime game against the Chiefs.

Shavers played 27 offensive snaps and 16 special-teams in his return to the field Sunday. The wide receiver has finally started to mix into the offense after recovering from the torn ACL he suffered in the Bills' 27-24 wild-card win over the Jaguars last January.

Johnson did not carry the rock much at all in the contest. The running back did, however, rank third in receiving yards for Buffalo behind Khalil Shakir (101) and DJ Moore (91). Johnson should continue to see receiving opportunities in Week 12 against the Chiefs as the Bills' preferred third-down back.

With Dalton Kincaid (thumb) inactive, Latu moved a rung up on the ladder at tight end and ended up seeing his most extensive playing time on offense of the season, logging 28 of 78 snaps (36 percent). He parlayed the elevated snaps into a season-high target count, but Latu's lone reception actually came on special teams, when Tommy Doman faked a punt and connected with the 24-year-old deep down the field for a fourth-down conversion. Latu will likely see his opportunities take a hit if Kincaid makes it back for a Thursday matchup with the Chiefs in Week 12.

Bass was able to make at least three field goals for the fifth time in the team's last six contests. The kicker made field goals from 43 and 54 yards in the first half before adding makes from 40 and 28 yards in the fourth quarter. His lone miss of the day came in the third quarter, when he pulled a 54-yard try wide left, registering his first missed field-goal try of the year. Bass has now gone 24-for-25 on field-goal attempts, including 4-for-5 from 50-plus yards, over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

Evans took a step in the right direction by practicing to some extent Friday after being listed as non-participant on Thursday's estimate. He'll have one more chance to reach full participation Saturday ahead of Monday's game against the Buccaneers. Evans had his best game of the season in the Week 11 win over Baltimore, catching all five of his targets for 44 yards and his first touchdown of the season.

Tremble was limited again Friday after being listed a limited participant on Thursday's practice estimate. He has one more opportunity to upgrade to full participation Saturday, which could help Tremble avoid an injury designation for Monday's game against the Buccaneers.

Brooks has shed any practice limitations, but he would still need to be added back to the active roster to play Monday in Tampa Bay. Even if Brooks gets the green light to suit up and is activated by the Panthers, he would likely have to settle for a change-of-pace role behind Chuba Hubbard against Tampa Bay's excellent run defense.

Waller was among four Panthers tight ends to have a capped session Friday, the others being Tommy Tremble (knee), Mitchell Evans (Achilles) and Feleipe Franks (wrist). Waller was able to play through his knee injury this past Sunday against the Ravens, when he handled a 46 percent snap share en route to three catches (on three targets) for 42 yards.

Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reported earlier Friday that McMillan was in a helmet and pads, and although he ditched them while stretching he put them back on shortly afterward. Ultimately, Friday's injury report will include McMillan's activity level, if any, after he was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's practice estimate due to a sore foot.

Okereke is in danger of missing a third consecutive game as he continues to deal with a knee injury suffered during Week 8. If he ends up being unable to play in Monday's matchup versus the Buccaneers, Tyrel Dodson will likely get another start at inside linebacker.

Incoom was placed on injured reserve in late October due to a calf injury that he sustained in Week 6 against the Eagles. Regardless of his practice participation over the next three days, the Panthers would have to activate Incoom from injured reserve in order for him to be available for Monday's NFC South tilt against the Buccaneers.

Dodson came up big for the Panthers in the win, forcing two turnovers, including a game-clinching  interception of Jacoby Brissett late in the fourth quarter. The 28-year-old has now totaled seven or more tackles in three consecutive games and he will look to maintain this level of production during the Week 12 matchup versus the Buccaneers.

injuries.evidence: Christensen has been rehabbing from a hamstring injury all year, but he was not activated from IR within 21 days of returning to practice, so he'll now miss the rest of the season.
injuries.detail: Christensen has been rehabbing from a hamstring injury all year, but he was not activated from IR within 21 days of returning to practice, so he'll now miss the rest of the season. The veteran guard will now have to look forward to hopefully returning at some point in 2027.

The four tackles matched Lloyd's season low in a game this season, which he's done three times in nine contests. While he doesn't post huge tackle numbers, Lloyd makes noise in other areas of the box score. He's piled up 67 tackles (39 solo), including 2.5 sacks, and five pass breakups, including three interceptions, on 94 percent of the defensive snaps in 2026.

The wide receiver did play nine snaps on special teams. Legette missed six games with a knee injury before returning for Carolina's win over the Saints in Week 10, though he only saw action on two offensive snaps in that contest. Legette has two catches for 64 yards and no touchdowns in four games this season.

Metchie and Bryce Young connected on a 19-yard pass late in the third quarter to set the Panthers up in the red zone, and the drive ended four plays later on a 33-yard field goal by Ryan Fitzgerald. Metchie has caught one pass in each of his last two outings, and the fifth-year pro is firmly behind Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker on the wide-receiver depth chart. The Panthers will hit the road in Week 12 for a crucial NFC South clash against the Buccaneers on Monday, Nov. 30.

Etienne did it all in Week 11 while only playing 10 offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps. Despite the modest playing time, the running back made an impact across the box score. Etienne continues to be the reserve option behind bell-cow back Chuba Hubbard, whose role is as entrenched as any player at his position in the league.

Fitzgerald was able to make multiple field-goal tries for the second straight week and seventh time overall this season. The kicker made a 33-yard field goal in the third quarter before he converted a 37-yarder with 1:44 left in the fourth quarter, ultimately putting the Panthers in front 35-33. Fitzgerald now has gone 17-for-19 on field-goal attempts, including 5-for-5 from 50-plus yards, while converting 21 of 26 extra-point tries over 10 contests so far during the 2026 season.

Horn is currently considered day-to-day, but head coach Dave Canales wants to ensure Horn is in a great head space before returning. The 2021 first-round pick has been sidelined since late September, while Chau Smith-Wade has handled slot-cornerback duties in his absence. The Panthers will still have to officially activate Horn off injured reserve before he's eligible to return.

Coker endured a helmet-to-helmet hit at the end of a six-yard catch in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win against the Ravens, getting shaken up in the process. Afterward, be reportedly entered the concussion protocol, but one day later he doesn't have a head injury. Coker thus is in the clear ahead of next Monday's game at Tampa Bay.

The fourth-year QB posted his best single-game completion rate of the season (73.3 percent) while tossing multiple TDs for the third time in the last six contests, a stretch in which he's compiled a 9:5 TD:INT. Both of Young's scores came in the first half, as he connected with Mitchell Evans on a 23-yard TD and Tetairoa McMillan on a seven-yard strike. Young will look to keep rolling in Week 12 against Tampa Bay.

Loveland is seeking a second opinion on a knee injury he sustained in Chicago's 39-35 win over the Lions on Thanksgiving. Even if initial fears of a stint on IR prove overblown, Loveland is still considered week-to-week and could be in line for a multi-game absence, starting with Week 13 against the Jaguars. Since Cole Kmet (knee) is on IR, Roush and Stephen Carlson are Chicago's only healthy options at TE. Roush had five catches on as many targets for 31 yards after Loveland's early exit Thursday.

Schefter reported earlier that the Bears planned to place Loveland on injured reserve due to the knee injury the TE sustained in Thursday's 39-35 win over the Lions, which would rule Loveland out for at least four weeks. Chicago wants to gather more information before a determination is made on Loveland's status, and the door is still open for a shorter absence, though it would be surprising at this point if he's able to play Dec. 6 against the Jaguars.

Carlson hadn't caught a pass across his previous three appearances this season but benefited from increased playing time after Colston Loveland (knee) exited the game in the first quarter. Carlson could continue to see increased usage if Loveland is forced to miss extended time.

Raymond had a solid outing against his former team, as he finished tied for fourth on the Bears in receptions. The 32-year-old has now caught 36 passes for 324 yards and a touchdown, in addition to racking up 209 punt-return yards across 11 games this season.
Santos' lone field goal came from 40 yards out during the victory. The 35-year-old has converted 18 of his 22 field-goal attempts and 33 of his 34 extra-point tries across 11 games this season.

The third-year wideout played hero in the fourth quarter on Thanksgiving. With the Bears down 35-24, Odunze hauled in a 41-yard strike from Caleb Williams (abdomen)  and then went up for a six-yard score in the back corner of the end zone with just three seconds left on the clock. Odunze sports a 42-660-3 line on 64 targets through 11 games, and if Colston Loveland (knee) ends up missing more time after exiting Thursday's game early, there could be more looks available for him in a Week 13 tilt against the Jaguars.

The second-year wideout has taken a back seat to Rome Odunze coming out of Chicago's Week 10 bye. While Burden has managed just a 5-54-0 line on 10 targets over the last two games, Odunze topped those numbers on Thanksgiving alone with a 6-87-2 line on nine targets. Burden still has better overall numbers on the season, but the gap is closing rapidly. Colston Loveland (knee) left Thursday's game early, however, which could open up more volume for both of the Bears' top WRs. Burden will look to get rolling in Week 13 against the Jaguars.

Once again Monangai took a back seat to D'Andre Swift in terms of volume, but he punched in rushing scores from one and two yards out. The junior member of the Bears' backfield is up to five TDs on the season in six games, all on the ground, and Monangai's goal-line role keeps him fantasy-relevant heading into a Week 13 clash with the Jaguars.

While Kyle Monangai swooped in to score two TDs at the goal line, Swift put up impressive numbers of his own, leading the Bears in both rushing and receiving yards while hitting paydirt on a 30-yard run in the third quarter. The seven grabs and 97 receiving yards were both season highs for Swift, and the added volume came as a result of Colston Loveland's early exit due to a knee injury. If Loveland ends up missing more time, Swift's usage as a pass catcher could get a boost again in Week 13 against the Jaguars. He's already been plenty busy on that front this season, and through 11 contests he's compiled 959 scrimmage yards and a career-high 12 total TDs (10 rushing, two receiving).

Williams seemingly went for a precautionary X-ray after Week 12 action due to a "weird fall" that occurred during Thursday's contest in which he engineered two TD drives in the final 8:20 of the fourth quarter to eke out a four-point victory. He completed 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions and recorded three carries for 15 yards. With plenty of time to recover before the Bears' next game Sunday, Dec. 6 against the Jaguars, Williams has a decent chance to avoid practice restrictions next week.

Jackson dealt with an elbow issue through the short week of prep, but he's going to suit up Thursday. After playing a significant role on defense early in the campaign, the veteran linebacker has logged all but one of his snaps on special teams over Chicago's past three games, and that will likely continue to be his role against Detroit.

Stevenson was a late addition to the injury report Wednesday as a limited practice participant due to a groin issue. However, he'll be able to push through the injury and suit up against Detroit. That's significant for the Bears, as Stevenson is tied for second on the team with five defensed passes this season.

Keenum will fill the Bears' emergency quarterback role for a sixth consecutive week. He'll be able to enter Thursday's contest only if both Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent have to exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

The cornerback didn't practice at all this week and will miss a second straight game after he was injured in Week 9 against the Bucs. Clark Phillips handled third cornerback duties in last Sunday's win over the Saints.

Roschon Johnson (ankle) was ruled out for Thursday's game, leaving the Bears with only two healthy options in the backfield going into Thanksgiving. With that, Ahmed will be up from the practice squad for the divisional tilt against the Lions.

Johnson injured his ankle in Sunday's win over the Saints, and with the quick turnaround for Week 12, he won't be available against the Lions. The Bears will roll with D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai as their only healthy backs for Thursday's game.

Playing in his 85th career regular-season game, Lewis' first-quarter sack of Tyler Shough on third-and-11 was the first of the safety's career. Lewis has started eight of the nine games in which he's appeared this season, logging 42 tackles (30 solo) and two pass breakups, including an interception.

Thieneman picked off Tyler Shough in New Orleans' territory in the second quarter, and the Bears turned it into a touchdown three plays later to go up 16-0. It was Thieneman's second interception of the season. The rookie safety is up to 64 tackles (34 solo), including 1.5 sacks, and six pass breakups across 10 games.

Picked up from the Titans ahead of the trade deadline, Simmons has been everything the Bears could've imagined and then some in three games with his new team. He's up to 14 tackles (nine solo), including 5.0 sacks, and a pair of pass breakups since joining Chicago.

Thomas was cleared to play Sunday after working through an ankle issue that prevented him from practicing Friday. The ankle didn't appear to bother him, as he turned his first touch of the game into a 30-yard rush midway through the second quarter before connecting with Caleb Williams for 40 and 16 yards in the third and fourth quarters, respectively. It was the rookie third-round wideout's best performance of the season, and while Chicago boasts talented pass catchers like Luther Burden, Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland, Thomas' big-play potential could be something that the Bears lean into for Thanksgiving Day against the Lions, whose defense ranks 27th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (233.1) and 29th in passing touchdowns allowed (21).

injuries.detail: Iosivas had his 21-day window to return from IR opened Nov. 12, so the Bengals are running out of time to add him back to the active roster before he would need to miss the remainder of the season. If Iosivas isn't added back onto the roster ahead of Sunday's game, expect such a move to transpire early the following week before the Bengals travel to Cleveland. Dohnte Meyers has been filling in as Cincinnati's No. 3 WR during Iosivas' ongoing absence.

Higgins wasn't on the Bengals' Week 12 injury report until Friday, but after missing the team's final practice, the wideout's status is now worth tracking ahead of Sunday's 1:00 pm ET kickoff. While a late-week downgrade in practice participation like this can't be ignored, Ben Baby of ESPN.com notes that "Higgins just woke up with some soreness" Friday and that the team gave the WR the day to work through it." More importantly, Baby indicates that the issue isn't a concern in terms of Higgins' availability versus New Orleans.
out

Dugger has apparently overcome his quadriceps injury after being declared inactive for Monday night's loss to the Commanders. The reserve safety is set to practice in full capacity through Week 12 prep ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints.

Endries reeled in a career-high four passes while playing 15 snaps on offense in Week 11. The rookie is still behind Mike Gesicki and Drew Sample in the pecking order at tight end ahead of Week 12 versus the Saints.

Young reeled in his first pass since Week 3, and he notched his first career touchdown in the process. The wide receiver connected with quarterback Joe Burrow for a four-yard score in the third quarter, momentarily providing Cincinnati with a 17-10 lead. Young's 22 offensive snaps ranked third at his position behind Ja'Marr Chase (56) and Tee Higgins (56) while ahead of Dohnte Meyers (21), but Young may revert to a smaller role on offense with Andrei Iosivas (thumb) on track to return in Week 12.

After catching a touchdown pass from Joe Burrow in Week 10 against the Steelers, Sample saw only one target from the superstar quarterback during Monday's loss. Sample has caught one pass or zero in seven of 10 regular-season games and has an 11-72-2 receiving line on 12 targets while operating as the Bengals' TE2 behind Mike Gesicki.

After both teams went scoreless in a rainy first quarter, McPherson put the Bengals on the board with a 38-yard field goal in the second. He nailed a 56-yarder late in the fourth to give the Bengals a 20-19 lead, but his would-be game winner didn't come to pass as the Commanders raced down the field to set up Drew Stevens for a 26-yard field goal to seal the win for Washington. McPherson has made only five field goals (on six attempts) over the Bengals' last five games, but his 35 point-afters are second-most in the NFL behind Eddy Pineiro (36). The Bengals will head back home for Week 12 against the Saints, whose defense ranks 23rd in the NFL in points allowed per game (25.7).

Most of Meyers' production came on special teams as a returner, and his one catch was his fewest since Week 7 against the Ravens, when he failed to record a reception. He's caught two passes or fewer in seven of 10 regular-season games, and his minimal role on offense would shrink even more once Andrei Iosivas (thumb) is cleared to return from injured reserve. The Bengals will head home for Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.

The Commanders' defense focused its attention toward slowing down both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. That opened up the field for Perine, with most of his production coming on a 44-yard catch late in the second quarter, and the drive ended two plays later with a 31-yard touchdown pass from Joe Burrow to Higgins. Perine finished second on the Bengals in both catches and receiving yards behind tight end Mike Gesicki, and the RB's 26 rushing yards were well ahead of Chase Brown's six. Perine has at least 10 touches in each of his last three games, but Cincinnati's offense is mustering only 79.4 rushing yards per game, which is third-worst in the NFL. Given Brown's struggles this season, Perine could take on a larger role in the backfield for Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.

The veteran tight end finished with a team-high yardage total while coming just a yard short of equaling his best tally of the season as well. Gesicki's biggest catch came late in the fourth quarter on the Bengals' final drive, when he hauled in a 32-yard pass from Joe Burrow over the middle to get the Bengals down to  the Commanders' 33-yard line. Gesicki's production continues to have some game-to-game volatility, but he'll draw another favorable matchup in a Week 12 home clash with the Saints on Sunday.

As his final line indicates, Brown was completely stonewalled by a talented Commanders run defense, although backfield mate Samaje Perine, who equaled Brown's carry total, was able to average 4.3 yards per tote with his opportunities and  added 71 receiving yards. Brown did find a way to make his usual impact as a receiver, tying for the team lead in receptions and finishing second in targets to Ja'Marr Chase. Brown's carry and rushing yardage totals were both season lows, but he should have appreciably better conditions for production on the ground in a Week 12 home matchup against the Saints on Sunday.

The Commanders focused on keeping Chase in check after his 231-yard outburst against the Steelers in Week 10, and they executed that plan to near perfection. The superstar wideout finished with his third-lowest yardage total of the season, and his sparsest since Week 4. Chase still extended his streak of five-plus-catch efforts to six games, and he'll look to bounce back to his usual level of production in a Week 12 home matchup against a vulnerable Saints defense Sunday.

The Bengals offense started slowly and was shut out altogether in the first quarter, but Burrow was able to lead his team to 10 second-quarter points partly via a 31-yard touchdown pass to Tee Higgins. The prolific signal-caller added a four-yard scoring toss to Colbie Young in the third quarter, and Burrow then helped lead Cincinnati downfield for a go-ahead Evan McPherson 56-yard field goal with 46 seconds remaining, albeit after narrowly avoiding an interception and then taking a third-down sack. Nevertheless, the Bengals came up short when Jayden Daniels led the Commanders on a five-play, 64-yard game-winning march, but Burrow finished with his fourth tally of at least 300 passing yards this season. He'll look to put his team back in the win column in a favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Saints on Sunday.
The safety suffered a right ankle injury late in the first half and was questionable to return. Now that he's back, he should be able to resume his role in the lineup at free safety.

Parker had been on IR all season due to a knee injury but was added back to the 53-man roster after turning in five consecutive full practices upon having his 21-day evaluation window opened Nov. 12. He'll serve as a depth option at guard during Monday's contest.

Bozeman was designated for return from IR on Thursday and needed just three full practices before the Bengals were comfortable adding him back to the 53-man roster. While serving mainly as a special-teams contributor, Bozeman tallied four tackles through the first five weeks of the season before landing on IR due to a broken forearm.

Hill was absent from practice for the entire week due to an illness, but he is now good to go for Monday Night Football. The 26-year-old will operate in his starting role at slot cornerback versus Washington.

Davis strung together multiple full practices since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 12, but he still drew the doubtful tag for Monday's game. He'll end up missing a seventh consecutive game due to a hamstring injury, and his next chance to return is Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.

injuries.detail: Burks has been working through a groin issue for the past couple of weeks, and he aggravated the injury during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday. His placement on IR means he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 20.

With the Bengals having built their lead to 20 by the midway point of the fourth quarter, head coach Zac Taylor pulled starter Joe Burrow from the contest and turned to Flacco to run down the clock in the win. The appearance was Flacco's third of the season, but the veteran signal-caller still has yet to attempt a pass.

Coach Todd Monken noted Friday that the team pushed Boston (who was deemed a 'DNP' at practice over the last few days) pretty hard earlier in the week, then pulled back a little bit, while adding that the Browns should have a better idea regarding the wide receiver's Week 12 status Saturday. If Boston ends up out or limited this weekend, Malachi Corley, Tylan Wallace and Isaiah Bond would be in line to see added opportunities behind KC Concepcion and Jerry Jeudy.

Sanders was designated to return from injured reserve Tuesday, and he would need to be added to the active roster with an official transaction prior to Sunday's game to have a chance to play. Even if Sanders gets the green light, he's unlikely to see much action on offense, with Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson and Jaleel McLaughlin all healthy in Cleveland's backfield.
out

Whiteheart popped up on the injury report Wednesday due to a hip issue but should be good to go for Sunday's matchup versus the Raiders. The 26-year-old tight end has caught four of his seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown across 10 games this season.

The Browns didn't hold a practice on Thanksgiving Day, but the fact that Fannin was estimated as a full participant Thursday indicates that the second-year tight end is on track to play against the Raiders on Sunday. Fannin has caught at least six passes in three of his last four outings, and has compiled a 25-378-1 receiving line on 32 targets over that span.

Campbell's three defended passes matched his season total heading into the contest. The cornerback's biggest moment of the day was intercepting C.J. Stroud at the Cleveland 24-yard line with 48 seconds left in the first half. Campbell's turnover likely stole at least three points from the Texans in a game that was decided by the same swing.

Schwesinger continues to be a model of consistency, having played all 658 defensive snaps for the Browns in 2026. The middle linebacker has logged double-digit tackles in six of the team's 10 contests so far, adding 3.0 sacks and three forced fumbles over that span.

Corley had not caught a pass across the first nine games of the campaign before hauling in three passes during Sunday's victory. He ended up finishing the contest third on the team in receiving yards behind Harold Fannin and Jerry Jeudy.

Wallace again played a rotational role in Week 10, logging 13 snaps at wide receiver. He was able to draw a season-high two targets and come down with both of them, making him one of eight Browns to catch a pass from quarterback Deshaun Watson Sunday. Barring an injury to one of the wideouts ahead of him on the depth chart, he doesn't have a clear path to more consistent playing time following Cleveland's bye in Week 11.

Szmyt knocked through field goals from 49 and 26 yards in Sunday's contest. The kicker stumbled in the fourth quarter, missing a 54-yard attempt with 11:02 remaining that would've brought the game within a point. Szmyt is now 21-for-24 on field-goal attempts and 15-for-16 on PATs over 10 regular-season contests in 2026.

Since Week 7, McLaughlin has logged just three snaps on offense in the Browns' ensuing three games, but prior to Sunday, he still appeared to be in the mix for work on kickoff returns. However, Isaiah Bond and Malachi Corley have since taken over as the team's preferred kickoff returners, leaving McLaughlin without a role on special teams. McLaughlin will likely continue to see little use as Cleveland's No. 3 back behind Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson.

Sampson hardly carries the ball for Cleveland and is merely the pass-catching complement to Quinshon Judkins out of the backfield. Across five games this season, Sampson has rushed 19 times for 79  yards while adding 16 catches for 152 yards on 22 targets. He's playable in PPR fantasy leagues as a desperation RB2 option, particularly in games for which the Browns are projected to play from behind.

Jeudy boosted his final line considerably on a 65-yard connection with Deshaun Watson in the second period. Watson carried the ball into the end zone on the following snap to bring the Browns to within seven points. Jeudy's 74 receiving yards were a season-high mark, though he finished with two or fewer receptions for the third straight week. The veteran wideout is behind both WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, not to mention tight end Harold Fannin, in the pass-catcher pecking order, so he may need to rely on big plays to have a chance to make an impact for fantasy managers.

Concepcion finished second on the Browns in targets behind tight end Harold Fannin, who had nine. However, whereas Fannin was able to turn his looks into seven receptions and 91 yards, Concepcion posted a much more modest 3-21-0 line. The rookie wideout departed to the medical tent during the first half of the game due to an undisclosed issue, but he was able to quickly return. Concepcion hasn't put up prolific numbers this season, but he does have at least three receptions in eight of his 10 appearances. Cleveland is on bye in Week 11, so Concepcion will next suit up Sunday, Nov. 29, against Las Vegas.

Watson helped the Browns overcome a 17-point first-half deficit, even though he didn't throw any touchdown passes for the fourth straight game. The veteran signal-caller did pile up the passing yardage against his old team, however, eclipsing 300 yards for the third straight game in the process. Watson also hit Harold Fannin with a critical 30-yard pass on his last pass attempt of the afternoon to set up Quinshon Judkins' game-winning rushing touchdown, and he'll next draw a highly favorable matchup against the Raiders in a Week 12 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 29, following a Week 11 bye.

Williams recorded four tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, before leaving late in the fourth quarter due to back spasms. He was not cleared to return to Thursday's game, but there doesn't appear to be much concern over his status for Week 13 given the extended time between games.

Spann-Ford served as the team's starting tight end for the third consecutive game as Jake Ferguson remains sidelined with a knee injury. However, Spann-Ford had a quiet outing but will look to play a larger role next week versus the Seahawks if Ferguson is out again.

Aubrey missed a kick from 40 yards out in the fourth quarter, which ended up being the difference in the game. The 31-year-old has now converted 21 of his 26 field-goal attempts and 36 of his 38 extra-point tries across 12 games this season and will look to bounce back during next week's matchup against the Seahawks.

It was a step back for Pickens after he hauled in 18 of 28 targets for 247 yards and four TDs over the prior two games. The 25-year-old wideout is the clear No. 2 option in the Dallas passing attack behind CeeDee Lamb, but the team's woeful defense and limited depth behind the duo ensures that Pickens will see big volume from Dak Prescott more often than not. Pickens will take a 62-847-6 line on 99 targets into a Week 13 clash with the Seahawks.

He was once again Dak Prescott's top downfield option, leading the Cowboys in targets, catches and receiving yards, but KaVontae Turpin and Javonte Williams were on the other end of the QB's touchdown passes. Lamb has topped 100 yards in six of 12 games this season, including three of the last four, and he'll carry a 95-1,242-9 line on 144 targets into a tough Week 13 battle against the Seahawks.

All three scores came in the first half as the Cowboys raced out to a 28-10 lead, making Williams the first player with three TDs in a half on Thanksgiving since Brian Westbrook accomplished the feat with Philly in 2008. Williams is also the second RB in Cowboys history to have multiple games in a season with three or more scores, something Emmitt Smith pulled off in four separate campaigns. He's also reached 100 rushing yards in three of the last six games, and he's topped 1,000 yards from scrimmage for the second straight year in Dallas. Williams will look to keep rolling in Week 13 against the Seahawks.

The Cowboys held a 28-10 lead at the half and were up 38-24 early in the fourth quarter, but abysmal efforts by the defense and special teams squandered Prescott's third straight game producing at least three touchdowns. It was the first time since Week 8 that he failed to reach 300 passing yards, but the 33-year-old QB is still on course for a career-best campaign. He'll take a 27:7 TD:INT, along with three rushing scores, into a much tougher Week 13 tilt against the Seahawks.

Thompson last suited up in Week 3 against the Ravens in Rio de Janeiro, as he's missed the last two months due to a hamstring injury that required an IR stint. He likely will slot back in as the Cowboys' starting strong safety in Week 12.

Moore strung together three consecutive full practices during Week 12 prep, but he would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Thanksgiving Day. The rookie fourth-rounder has yet to make his 2026 regular-season debut due to a hip injury that he picked up in training camp.

Hip and groin injuries prevented Barham from playing in Week 11 against the Titans, but his full session Wednesday was enough for him to avoid a designation for Thanksgiving Day. The rookie third-rounder has accumulated 37 tackles (21 solo) and one forced fumble through 10 regular-season games.

Locke entered the league's concussion protocol following the Cowboys' Week 9 win over the Colts. He hasn't progressed enough in his recovery to return for Thanksgiving Day and will thus miss a third consecutive game. Locke's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Seahawks on Monday, Dec. 7.

Mingo's absence for Thanksgiving Day will be his third missed game in a row due to an ankle injury that he sustained in Week 9 against the Colts. His absence means KaVontae Turpin and Camden Brown will continue to operate in rotational roles on offense behind CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy. Mingo's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Seahawks on Monday, Dec. 7.

Winters suffered a knee injury against the Titans on Sunday, but his full practice Wednesday was enough for him to avoid a designation ahead of Thanksgiving Day. The fourth-year linebacker has accumulated 45 tackles (30 solo), one interception and one fumble recovery across nine regular-season games.

The running back will again be active as Javonte Williams' backup after rushing five times for 32 yards, adding one catch for five yards on one target, across 18 offensive snaps last Sunday against the Titans.

The No. 11 overall pick in the 2026 Draft, Downs has started all 11 games this season and has piled up 73 tackles (40 solo), including 2.0 sacks, three pass breakups, including an interception, and two forced fumbles on 92 percent of the Cowboys' defensive snaps.

The second-year linebacker has started each of the last five games for Dallas and has played at least 88 percent of the defensive snaps in all of them. With Dee Winters (knee) injured against Tennessee, James should remain in the starting lineup Thursday against the Eagles. James has 44 tackles (28 solo), one interception and a fumble recovery across 11 contests this season.

The fifth-year edge rusher entered Sunday with 1.5 sacks on the season, so he more than doubled that number with his big game. With Malachi Lawrence (ankle) on injured reserve, Houston's snaps have been dialed up over the last three games. Through seven contests this season, Houston has 18 tackles (nine solo), including 3.5 sacks, and six QB hits.

With Jake Ferguson (knee) remaining out for Dallas, Schoonmaker played 25 of 65 offensive snaps behind Brevyn Spann-Ford. Schoonmaker ran 12 routes, five fewer than Spann-Ford, and the duo combined to see three targets on a day Dak Prescott attempted 33 passes. Schoonmaker has five catches for 48 yards on six targets across nine games this season and has no fantasy appeal.

injuries.evidence: Bland was placed on injured reserve Sunday after suffering an ankle injury during the Week 10 loss to the 49ers, but the injury is not expected to be season-ending.
injuries.detail: Bland was placed on injured reserve Sunday after suffering an ankle injury during the Week 10 loss to the 49ers, but the injury is not expected to be season-ending. The earliest Bland will be eligible to make his return is the Week 16 matchup versus Jacksonville, and Ameer Speed and Cobie Durant should continue to see increased playing time in his absence.

The fifth-year tight end was one of eight pass catchers that quarterback Dak Prescott connected with on the afternoon, with the pair of receptions marking Mitchell's first two grabs of the season. Mitchell took the field for 15 of the Cowboys' 65 snaps on offense, but he could wind up seeing most of his playing time on special teams once top tight end Jake Ferguson is cleared to return from the knee injury that has sidelined him for the past two games.

The Cowboys' slot receiver drew just one look on Dak Prescott's 33 pass attempts. He'd caught multiple passes in all 10 games leading up to Sunday's contest. A favorite target of Prescott in the red zone, Flournoy will try to rebound at home against the Eagles on Thanksgiving, when he'll be playable on three-game fantasy slates for Thursday.

Turpin went without a catch for the fourth time this season, but he was able to make his mark as a rusher in Week 11. The wideout was able to break loose for a 22-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter, notching his second score on the ground this season. Turpin has now caught five of 11 targets for 49 yards, rushed five times for 60 yards and two touchdowns, and added 695 kick-return yards and 121 yards as a punt returner over eight contests so far during the 2026 season.
Ehlinger won't get into any Black Friday action unless both Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham get hurt or are ejected in Denver's Week 12 tilt against the Steelers.

Badie was activated from injured reserve Thursday and will make his return Friday, likely working in a change-of-pace role behind Jonah Coleman while J.K. Dobbins is suspended. Cody Shrader is also on the roster at running back, while RJ Harvey (knee) could be activated from IR himself as soon as Week 13 against the Dolphins.

injuries.evidence: Jones had previously been ruled out for Friday's matchup versus the Steelers but will now be forced to miss at least four games before he's eligible to return.
injuries.detail: Jones had previously been ruled out for Friday's matchup versus the Steelers but will now be forced to miss at least four games before he's eligible to return. In his absence, Tyler Onyedim should be in line for increased playing time.

Schrader reached the maximum three games of elevation from the practice squad, but now that he's on the active roster, the Missouri product is eligible to suit up for the Broncos moving forward. He's expected to contribute as a kickoff returner, and Schrader could also settle in as the No. 2 or 3 running back behind starter Jonah Coleman in Friday's game against the Steelers with J.K. Dobbins serving a one-game suspension.

Lohner was a full participant in all three practice sessions during Week 12 prep. However, the second-year pro is not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve, so his next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6. Lohner is in the final stages of his recovery from a procedure on his foot in June.

Head coach Sean Payton had previously announced Tuesday that Dobbins would be suspended for Friday's game against the Steelers due to conduct detrimental to the team, but it wasn't immediately clear whether or not the running back would count toward the 53-man roster. As a result of Wednesday's transaction, the Broncos will now have an open roster spot to use for Week 12, and Tyler Badie (thumb) could be activated from injured reserve to help fill the void in the backfield. Dobbins' suspension came after he played just one snap in the Broncos' 38-24 win over the Raiders on Sunday, when rookie Jonah Coleman took on a bell-cow role and handled 28 touches.

Jones has missed the team's last two games while nursing a hamstring injury, but he now appears to be all set to return to action Friday against the Steelers. The 28-year-old will have a couple more chances to officially practice before potentially returning to his starting role at free safety in Week 12.

Tuesday was Denver's first practice, and given Elliss's absence, he's highly unlikely to participate in any of the Broncos' next two sessions ahead of Black Friday. The third-year linebacker is recovering from an ankle injury that landed him on IR in late October. Assuming he doesn't play in Week 12, Elliss's next opportunity to play would be Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Singleton was able to notch double-digit stops for the fourth time in the last five games and sixth time overall this year. The linebacker also notched a sack for the third time in four weeks, getting to Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza for a 10-yard loss in the second quarter. Singleton is now up to 118 total tackles (54 solo), including 3.0 sacks, while also registering three passes defensed over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

McMillian had himself a day in Week 11, finishing second on the team in takedowns behind linebacker Alex Singleton (11). The cornerback was also able to strip Raiders running back Mike Washington in the third quarter, but Washington jumped on the loose ball. McMillian's biggest moment of the game came in the fourth quarter, however, when he notched a 35-yard pick-six on an outside pass from quarterback Fernando Mendoza with two minutes left in regulation. McMillian has now registered 39 total tackles (25 solo), including 3.0 sacks, while also adding two interceptions, including Sunday's pick-six, and a forced fumble over 10 contests this season.
The wide receiver did see two targets, but he wasn't able to haul them in. Franklin has just 17 targets across 10 games this year, recording nine catches for 100 yards and no scores.

Trautman leaked open behind Las Vegas' defense on a play-action pass from the goal line early in the second quarter, giving Denver a 10-0 lead. He still has a big role in the Broncos' offense, but he isn't running enough routes to sustain pass-catching production worth fantasy consideration in most formats.

Mims reeled in just one pass for the second straight game, but his 36-yard snag in the second quarter was enough to notch his second-highest receiving yardage total in a contest this year. The wideout played just 15 snaps on offense, which ranked fifth at his position behind Courtland Sutton (49), Pat Bryant (40), Jaylen Waddle (39) and Troy Franklin (24) for Denver in Week 11. Mims will remain an unappealing fantasy option ahead of Friday's matchup with the Steelers.

The veteran kicker now has gone five straight games without missing a kick, as he's 9-for-9 on field goals and 14-for-14 on extra points in that span. With the Denver offense heating up after a slow start to the campaign, Lutz has become useful in fantasy. On the season, he's 17-for-20 on FGAs and has made all 21 of his PATs.

Adkins was on the field for 30 of the Broncos' 73 snaps on offense, with his 41 percent share representing a season-high mark. The fourth-year tight end out of South Carolina has mainly served as a blocking specialist for Denver, having thus far been limited to a 7-47-3 receiving line on nine targets to go with a six-yard carry through 10 appearances on the season.

The wideout briefly exited the game in the third quarter after he appeared to tweak his previously injured ankle, but Bryant quickly returned and was able to finish out the contest. His four targets were fourth on the team on a day Bo Nix targeted nine different players on 35 pass attempts. The Denver offense spreads the ball around to five different receivers, three tight ends and its running backs most weeks, making it difficult for any of the pass catchers to post big numbers in the box score.

Sutton thus was blanked in the box score for the first time Week 7 of the 2024 campaign, a span of 39 games (including playoffs). Considering he's surpassed 50 receiving yards just one time in 10 appearances in 2026, he doesn't hold much sway for fantasy purposes, especially in a Broncos offense that often has sputtered this season. Sutton's next chance to turn the tide arrives Friday at Pittsburgh.

It was easily Engram's best performance of the season, as he set season highs in targets, catches and yards against Las Vegas. Entering Sunday, Engram had produced just seven grabs for 48 yards total over his previous four games. Engram and the Broncos have a quick turnaround ahead of Friday's date with the Steelers. The tight end will be a low-floor fantasy option for that one.

After a hit-or-miss first six appearances of the season, Nix has settled into a four-game stretch in which his passing yards have ranged from 222 to 237 weekly, a span in which he boasts a 6:2 TD:INT and 84 rushing yards and another score. He also displayed some promise with offseason acquisition Jaylen Waddle (3-61-0 on six targets) while connecting with TE Adam Trautman for his 12th touchdown pass in 10 contests. Nix will look to keep things rolling Friday at Pittsburgh.

Vaki once again filled a limited role as Jahmyr Gibbs continues to handle the bulk of the workload. The 25-year-old has totaled 181 rushing yards on 43 carries, in addition to catching 11 of his 13 targets for 84 yards across 11 games this season.

Bates' missed extra point came from 48 yards out due to a 15-yard taunting penalty. The 27-year-old has now converted 19 of his 21 field-goal attempts and 36 of his 37 extra-point tries across 11 games this season.

Despite the high score, Jared Goff threw only one TD pass on the afternoon, connecting with LaPorta for an 11-yard strike in the second quarter, The tight end snapped a five-game touchdown drought in the process, but he still hasn't topped four catches or 62 yards in six contests since Detroit's bye. LaPorta will take a 43-521-4 line on 64 targets through 11 games into a Week 13 clash with the Falcons.

The fifth-year wideout finished second on the Lions in targets, catches and receiving yards to Amon-Ra St. Brown (7-146-0 on 10 targets), a position that Williams is very used to finding himself in. Williams tied his season high in receptions with the performance, and he'll take a 42-679-6 line on 64 targets through 11 games into a Week 13 clash with the Falcons.

The veteran QB topped 300 passing yards for the fifth time this season, but Goff's only touchdown came on an 11-yard connection with Sam LaPorta in the second quarter, as Jahmyr Gibbs did most of the scoring for the Lions. Goff has thrown multiple TDs in just two of the last five games, a stretch in which he's managed a 7:5 TD:INT, but he could pop for a ceiling game in Week 13 against a struggling Falcons defense.

It was the third time this season St. Brown has hauled in more than 140 yards in a game, but he got shut out of the end zone as Jahmyr Gibbs did most of the scoring for the Lions. St. Brown has caught at least seven passes in four of the last six games, and through 11 contests he's racked up a 77-938-8 line on 107 targets. He'll look to reach 1,000 yards for the fifth straight season in Week 13 on the road against the Falcons.

The superstar running back was already headed for a career-best season coming into Week 12, but Gibbs took things to another level on Thanksgiving, producing his third career game with three rushing scores and his second with 200-plus rushing yards. The 252 scrimmage yards also tied his season high, a mark he reached just two weeks ago against the Patriots. Gibbs leads the NFL with 1,754 scrimmage yards, and given his current form he could reach 2,000 as soon as next week, on the road against the Falcons.
Ratledge had his lower leg rolled up on in the first quarter but was able to rejoin the lineup as the Lions' right guard one possession later.

Rodriguez has his ankle rolled up on in the third quarter and immediately made his way to the sideline tent before the Lions deemed him questionable to return. He had four tackles and a fumble recovery before his exit.

Wonnum was able to practice in a limited capacity Wednesday, but that didn't end up being enough for him to suit up Thursday. He leads the Lions with 7.0 sacks this season, so the veteran defensive end's absence is a big deal for Detroit. Tyler Lacy, Ahmed Hassanein, Eric O'Neill and Anthony Lucas could all be involved in trying to fill the void left by Wonnum's absence Thursday.

Clark dealt with a hamstring issue during Week 12 prep and is going to miss his first game of the campaign as a result. He's been a starter at safety for the Lions all season and played every defensive snap in three of Detroit's past four games. Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch will start at safety Thursday, with Andre Cisco working in reserve.
