injuries.evidence: Gill-Howard suffered a season-ending knee injury during the Lions' Week 11 win over the Buccaneers.
injuries.detail: Gill-Howard suffered a season-ending knee injury during the Lions' Week 11 win over the Buccaneers. The rookie sixth-rounder will finish his first NFL campaign with 11 tackles (two solo), including 2.0 sacks, across 10 regular-season games.

Branch played 98 percent of the Lions' defensive snaps in the contest. The strong safety has now had two passes defensed in consecutive weeks, totaling five in his five regular-season games in 2026. Sunday's game marked the first of 2026 that Branch and free safety Kirby Joseph played alongside each other, and they could certainly help shore up the back end of the defense down the stretch.

Ya-Sin played 59 defensive snaps in the contest and one snap on special teams. The cornerback played 91 percent of the team's defensive snaps, drawing the start due to the absence of Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder). Ya-Sin could see an elevated role again in Week 12 on Thursday against the Bears if Rakestraw remains sidelined.

Saylors didn't record any stats over two snaps on offense while recording 29 yards on his only kick return of the day in Week 11. The running back will continue to be unintriguing fantasy option while operating as an extreme depth option behind Jahmyr Gibbs and Sione Vaki in Detroit's backfield moving forward.

TeSlaa went without a reception for the second time in four weeks, and he has now gone six straight games without exceeding 20 receiving yards. The wide receiver played 23 snaps on offense, ranking third at his position behind Amon-Ra St. Brown (46) and Jameson Williams (45). TeSlaa will continue to be an unreliable fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 12 matchup with the Bears on Thursday.

One of Wright's two grabs in Week 11 was a 27-yard strike up the seam, easily his longest reception of the season thus far. He was on the field for 43 of the Lions' 58 offensive snaps Sunday, but he spent a substantial majority of those on blocking assignments for tailback Jahmyr Gibbs and company. His role in a Thanksgiving tilt versus the Bears may depend somewhat on the health of running mate Sam LaPorta, who was limited during Monday's walkthrough with an ankle issue.

Reed appears to be on track to return to action Thursday against the Bears after missing three straight games with a hip injury. The cornerback will have two more chances to officially practice ahead of Week 12.

Dorsey hurt his wrist early in Sunday's game and was initially deemed questionable to return. The veteran cornerback has since been able to re-enter the game, albeit with a club over the hand that he injured. Dorsey has been working in a rotational role at cornerback, logging a defensive snap share between 32 and 38 percent three straight weeks.

Lacy was limited in practice all week due to a shoulder injury, but he's been cleared to play in Sunday's home game. He's expected to take on an elevated role at defensive end in the absence of Aidan Hutchinson, who is out for the rest of the season due to a torn ACL. Lacy has accumulated 12 tackles (four solo) through nine regular-season games.

Neither of Smack's field goals were chip shots; he nailed a 54-yarder late in the first quarter and a 48-yarder late in the second. The rookie entered Wednesday having gone just 15-for-21 on FG tries over his first 10 NFL games, so his accuracy Wednesday may have given him some needed job security. The most impressive aspect of Smack's rookie campaign has been his big leg. Despite his overall struggles, he's gone 4-for-5 on FG tries from 50-plus yards away.

Moore continued to serve as Green Bay's primary kick and punt returner, but he logged just one snap on offense. That limited usage as a receiver was even more concerning for his fantasy outlook given that star wideout Christian Watson couldn't play at all in the second half due to a concussion. Moore did notch 14 targets over his first five games, but since returning in Week 10 from a stint on IR, he's played just one offensive snap over two contests.

Melton's carry was his first of the season, so he hasn't been a weapon in that regard. However, he did step up a bit as a receiver, notching multiple receptions for the first time since he logged a season-high three catches in Week 5. Melton's main role this season has been as a kick returner, so he's well off the fantasy radar.

It was another rough performance for Green Bay's ground game, which gained just 55 yards on 14 carries. Williams got two totes, and the wide receiver ended up atop the team's rushing leaderboard with 18 yards, ahead of RBs Kaleb Johnson (13 yards on eight carries) and MarShawn Lloyd (10 yards on one carry). Williams has consistently seen minor work out of the backfield this season, logging at least one carry (but no more than three) in all but one of his six appearances. That gives a small boost to his fantasy outlook, but he's yet to reach 50 receiving yards in a game this season, so Williams is a very risky fantasy play. However, he'd probably get a boost in that regard if Christian Watson (concussion), who exited late in the first half Wednesday and didn't return, isn't able to suit up in Week 13 against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Brooks and Kaleb Johnson split the workload pretty evenly at running back for Green Bay, with the former logging 19 offensive snaps and the latter 24. Meanwhile, MarShawn Lloyd tallied just three snaps on offense. Whereas Johnson led the group with eight carries, Brooks was by far the most active in the passing game, tying for the overall team lead with both his five targets and four receptions. He had just four catches over five games coming into Wednesday, so it remains to be seen if the bump in work as a pass catcher continues for Brooks moving forward. The entire breakdown of the Packers backfield could shift in Week 13 against the Saints if Josh Jacobs (finger) is ready to return to action.

After logging double-digit snaps in each of his first nine games of the season, Lloyd totaled just three offensive snaps Wednesday. In that context, his production was relatively efficient -- in fact, his 10-yard run on his lone carry put him just behind starting running back Kaleb Johnson, who tallied just 13 rushing yards on eight totes. With that said, it's hard to see a path to meaningful fantasy production for Lloyd if he doesn't get more opportunities, and he could be phased out of the game plan altogether if Josh Jacobs (finger) is able to return for the Packers' Week 13 matchup in New Orleans on Sunday, Dec. 6.

As his final numbers indicate, Johnson couldn't find any running room but was very productive with his one catch. The 2025 third-round pick of the Steelers was in the lead role once again with Josh Jacobs (finger) inactive, but Johnson couldn't come close to matching the encouraging rushing production he'd managed over the previous two games (24 carries, 110 yards, one TD). Jacobs is expected back for the Packers' Week 13 road matchup against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6, a development that would relegate Johnson to his more customary reserve role.

Love already had a daunting challenge coming in against a talented Rams secondary. It was made exponentially more difficult due to Christian Watson, to whom he threw his only touchdown pass of the night in the second quarter from six yards out, exiting the game for good late in the first half due to a possible concussion. The veteran signal-caller unsurprisingly scuffled throughout, and his two interceptions came in the second half while the game was still within reach for Green Bay. The game marked Love's first with multiple interceptions this season, as well as his third below 200 passing yards. Love will look to bounce back when the Packers return to action on the road against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Golden saw Christian Watson exit for good late in the first half due to a possible concussion, but the former still couldn't capitalize on a night when Jordan Love threw for a modest 198 yards and tossed two interceptions. Golden's yardage total tied for his second-lowest figure of the season, while Wednesday marked his first game without multiple receptions. Golden will look to bounce back in a Week 13 road matchup against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Kraft finished second in receptions and tied for the team lead in targets for the Packers on a night when Jordan Love threw for under 200 yards. The veteran tight end saw Christian Watson exit the game twice with thigh and head injuries in the first half, the latter issue forcing his exit for the rest of the game. Kraft recorded multiple receptions for the first time in three contests in the process, but his first-quarter fumble led to a Rams field goal. Kraft carries an unremarkable 40-394-3 line heading into a Week 13 road matchup against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6.
Prior to leaving, the linebacker recorded four tackles (two solo). Dani Dennis-Sutton and Brenton Cox will see an uptick in snaps off the edge for Green Bay.

The wideout hasn't cleared concussion checks and will miss the remainder of the Week 12 contest after he was injured at the end of the second quarter when Watson took a hit to the head from Kamren Kinchens. Look for J. Michael Sturdivant and Bo Melton to see increased snaps alongside Matthew Golden and Savion Williams with Watson sidelined.

Zeitler was unable to play against the Vikings in Week 10 due to triceps and ankle injuries, but the veteran offensive lineman has been cleared to play Wednesday. He should start at right guard while Travis Glover provides depth at the position.

Glover's practice reps were limited due to a shoulder injury, but the third-year pro was given the green light by medical staff to play Wednesday. He's started in five regular-season games, most recently in Week 10 against the Vikings, but he'll likely operate in a depth role at right guard behind starter Kevin Zeitler.

Rhyan suffered a high ankle sprain against the Lions in Week 7, which sidelined him for the Packers' following three games. He's been cleared by medical staff to play Wednesday, and Rhyan will reclaim his starting spot at center while John Williams reverts to a depth role.

Franklin drew the questionable tag for Wednesday's game following three consecutive limited practices. However, the veteran linebacker will end up missing a fifth consecutive game due to a hairline fracture in his shin that he suffered during a practice session in late October, so Ty'Ron Hopper will continue to operate in an elevated role on defense. Franklin's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Coming out of the Packers' Week 11 bye, head coach Matt LaFleur told Matt Schneidman of The Athletic on Saturday that he didn't expect Jacobs to play in Week 12, but he also gave the running back a "chance to prove" he can. Jacobs then was listed as limited on practice reports Sunday through Tuesday and tagged as questionable ahead of Wednesday's game. Such activity wasn't enough for Jacobs to get the all clear to suit up, meaning Green Bay's backfield will be manned by Kaleb Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks for a second consecutive contest.

Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Monday that Parsons gained clearance to return to action, but first the Packers needed to activate him from the reserve/PUP list, which came to pass Tuesday. Parsons was listed as questionable ahead of Wednesday's matchup, and he's now ready for his first game since Dec. 14, 2025, when he tore the ACL and meniscus in his left knee. Tom Pelissero of Netflix reported Wednesday that Parsons will play approximately 50 percent of the defensive snaps in his season debut.

The Packers' rookie cornerback is ready to go for Wednesday's game against the Rams after he exited Week 10 early against the Vikings. Cisse has started all 10 games this season, recording 38 tackles (26 solo), including 1.5 sacks, and nine pass breakups, including an interception, on 83 percent of the defensive snaps.

LaFleur acknowledged that Musgrove is still in the process of rehabbing the neck injury he sustained during OTAs in June, and the Packers haven't yet prepared for the tight end to resume practicing. Barring dramatic progress in his recovery over the next month, Musgrave looks like he'll be sidelined for the final season of his rookie deal before hitting free agency in the spring.

Williams played every single defensive snap in Week 10 and finished tied for the second-most tackles on the Packers behind Isaiah McDuffie (10). Williams has recorded at least eight stops in three of his last four outings and is up to 84 tackles (50 solo), including 1.0 sacks, eight pass defenses (including three interceptions) and a fumble recovery through 10 regular-season games. He is well on track to surpass 100 tackles for a second consecutive year.

Schultz practiced without limitations Friday, shedding any doubts about his availability after an illness limited his participation Thursday. The Ravens have allowed seven TDs to TEs, which is seventh-most in the NFL, but Schultz has scored only once all season and is coming off consecutive one-catch performances.

Boutte's absence will coincide with the return of Marvin Harrison (hamstring) from a two-game absence. Harrison will join Nico Collins, Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson while Boutte sits out due to an hip injury the latter sustained in last Thursday's win over the Colts, which subsequently prevented Boutte from practicing in any capacity during Week 12 prep. Boutte's next chance to take the field will be Dec. 6 at Pittsburgh.

Marks, who was inactive Nov. 19 against the Colts, logged 'full' listings at practice Wednesday through Friday, and has now gained clearance to rejoin the lineup after being sidelined for one game. Marks' Week 11 absence coincided with the return to action of fellow RB David Montgomery, and now that both backs are available for the first time since Week 5, look for Marks to see a noticeable dip in volume while sharing touches with Montgomery, who logged 26 carries versus Indianapolis.

Harrison has missed the Texans' last two contests, but after a limited practice Wednesday, the wideout's full participation Thursday sets the stage for him to return to action Sunday against the Ravens. Given Harrison's modest production over three outings since arriving in a trade with the Cardinals, he profiles as a speculative fantasy lineup option in Week 12, with Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and possibly Kayshon Boutte (hip, 'DNP' Thursday) also in Houston's WR mix.

With the return of Reed Blankenship to the starting lineup, Stewart was relegated to special teams. The strong safety played 17 snaps but did not appear in the box score.
To'oTo'o played 100 percent of the Texans' defensive snaps for the second straight week. The linebacker was on the field for all 48 plays, logging four solo tackles in the effort.

Anderson extended his NFL sacks lead to 11.5 in Thursday's contest. The pass rusher is amassing another strong season to contend for Defensive Player of the Year. Anderson finished 2025 with 12.0 sacks and is set to surpass that personal record this season.

Moreau's 30 offensive snaps were second among Texans tight ends behind Dalton Schultz's 34, yet it was Marlin Klein who led the position group with four catches (on as many targets) for 24 yards, including a 13-yard touchdown pass from C.J. Stroud late in the third quarter. Moreau is up to a 12-80-3 receiving line on 15 targets through 10 regular-season games and has caught one pass or zero in five of those contests. He doesn't have much fantasy appeal unless Schultz were to miss time.

Fairbairn's only field goal of the night was a 27-yarder with 15 seconds remaining in the first half. The kicker is 20-for-21 on field-goal attempts and 27-for-27 on PATs over 10 regular-season games so far in 2026.

With Woody Marks (concussion) inactive, Demercado played the complementary role behind lead back David Montgomery, who rushed 26 times for 107 yards in his return from a multi-week groin injury. Demercado was picked up off waivers from Dallas last month.

Hutchinson played 54 of 66 offensive snaps, second at wide receiver on the team behind Nico Collins' 59, and the former has been operating as the Texans' WR2 in terms of playing time for the last several weeks. By not scoring a touchdown Thursday night, Hutchinson snapped his personal three-game touchdown streak. For the season, he has 30 catches for 358 yards and three scores on 57 targets. He's on pace to set new career highs across the board.

Klein surprisingly outpaced veteran position mates Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau on the night, and the rookie second-round pick, whose only other career reception coming in was a 16-yard grab in Week 1, added his first career touchdown on a 13-yard catch in the third quarter. Given Klein had been a complete non-factor coming into the night, it's difficult to predict whether Thursday's production will have any carryover to a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

The speedy wideout finished tied for second in receptions for the Texans on a night when C.J. Stroud recorded completions to nine different targets overall. Dell has played an effective complementary role since making his return from a gruesome 2024 knee injury in Week 7, as he now has an 11-196-1 line and four catches of 20-plus yards across 18 targets heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Stroud's night got off to a rocky start when a deflected pass resulted in an interception on the Texans' opening drive, but the red-hot signal-caller was near perfect from that point forward. The 2023 first-round pick went on to toss three touchdown passes for the second straight game and multiple scores for the fifth consecutive contest overall. Stroud connected with Nico Collins (42 yards), Kayshon Boutte (24 yards) and Marlin Klein (13 yards) for his trio of scoring strikes, and he'll take a sparkling 22:4 TD:INT into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Facing a Colts defense down both Sauce Gardner (calf) and Charvarius Ward (knee), Collins looked primed for a big night early when he recorded a 42-yard touchdown grab to cap off Houston's second possession. However, C.J. Stroud proceeded to spread the ball around to nine different targets overall, leading to Collins tying his second-lowest reception tally and posting his third-lowest yardage total of the season. However, the star wideout did extend his touchdown streak to three games, and he'll next take aim at what has been an inconsistent Ravens secondary in a Week 12 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Making his return from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, Montgomery functioned as the clear lead back with Woody Marks (concussion) unavailable. The former put together the best rushing yardage total of his brief Texans tenure, handling his highest number of carries since Week 4 of his 2023 debut campaign with the Lions. Montgomery also was encouragingly involved in a complementary role in the passing game, and he'll now have some extra time to recover from Thursday's workload ahead of a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29. However, if Marks is able to clear concussion protocol ahead of that contest, Montgomery will see his touch count take a hit.

DJ Giddens is set to inherit change-of-pace duties behind Jonathan Taylor in McGowan's absence. McGowan, who injured his hamstring in the Week 11 loss to the Texans, will have a bye to heal before possibly returning against the Eagles in Week 14.

Ogletree was held out of Wednesday's practice due to a knee injury, but his full session Thursday puts the fifth-year tight end on track to play against the Giants on Sunday. Ogletree has a 4-21-0 receiving line on seven targets through 11 regular-season games and has not been targeted in three of his last four outings.

injuries.evidence: Curry was placed on the Colts' injured reserve Tuesday, and head coach Shane Steichen informed reporters Wednesday that the rookie sixth-rounder's wrist injury was severe enough for him to require season-ending surgery.
injuries.detail: Curry was placed on the Colts' injured reserve Tuesday, and head coach Shane Steichen informed reporters Wednesday that the rookie sixth-rounder's wrist injury was severe enough for him to require season-ending surgery. Curry will end his first NFL campaign with 26 tackles (14 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and two fumble recoveries across 11 regular-season games. His absence means Carl Lawson, Jaylahn Tuimoloau and George Gumbs are all in line for more rotational snaps at defensive end.

Taylor-Britt was a full participant in Wednesday's practice in what was his first session since suffering a groin injury in Week 7 against the Vikings. Even if he strings together two more full sessions, Taylor-Britt would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Giants.

Gardner did not play in the Colts' Week 11 loss to the Texans due to a calf injury. The cornerback has recovered since Thursday's contest and is all set to practice in full throughout Week 12 prep. Gardner's fellow starting cornerback Charvarius Ward (knee) also missed Week 11 and was a limited participant Wednesday, meaning the Colts could get both corners back for Sunday against the Giants.

Additionally, Pierce acknowledged that playing in Week 1 was a bit lofty, per Bowen, with the WR saying Wednesday that he was still managing some pain at that stage. In any case, Pierce indicated that he's confident that his current recovery plan will lead to a full return to health. When that will be remains to be seen, but the 2022 second-rounder is still on IR ahead of Week 12, with the Colts presumably not planning to rush him back given the team's 3-8 record in a campaign that's been marked by the team moving several key players ahead of the trade deadline.

Taylor is slated to take his first extended snaps alongside Richardson since the 2024 season, when the two started together 10 times. The threat that Richardson presented to defenses as a runner seemed to aid Taylor's own effectiveness, as the running back averaged 4.8 yards per carry and scored eight touchdowns over that 10-game stretch. Now two years later, the Colts have a much less formidable offensive line in place and few established pass-catching weapons that defenses need to hone in on, so Taylor will likely be hard-pressed to match the lofty production he previously achieved with Richardson under center. Additionally, the 3-8 Colts may be cognizant of not overworking Taylor amid a losing season, though the loss of top backup Seth McGowan (hamstring) for at least Week 12 may result in Taylor seeing a slight uptick in opportunities after he played fewer than 70 percent of snaps in each of the last five games and averaged 16.6 touches in those contests.

In a corresponding transaction, the Colts placed rookie sixth-round defensive end Caden Curry on injured reserve. In his one appearance so far this season back in Week 8 at Jacksonville, Lawson played just eight defensive snaps.

Buechele takes the QB No. 3 spot in Indy behind Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard. The 28-year-old spent the previous 11 weeks of the NFL season with Buffalo, splitting time on the active roster and practice squad.

Head coach Shane Steichen said Monday that McGowan "will miss some time" but didn't specify how long the absence may be. For however long McGowan is sidelined, Giddens figures to serve as Jonathan Taylor's backup at running back. Giddens has shown some flashes this season in limited playing time, amassing 48 yards on seven carries (6.9 YPC) and catching his only target for 11 yards over three games.

For the second week in a row, Brown ended up seeing more snaps on special teams (11) than offense. Through four games with Indianapolis, Brown has drawn just one target, which he turned into a seven-yard reception during a Week 6 loss to the Titans.

Boettcher finished Thursday's game tied for the fourth-most tackles on the Colts. The rookie fourth-rounder has started in each of Indianapolis' last three games, which has lined up with the absence of Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee, IR). Boettcher is up to 50 tackles (16 solo) through 11 regular-season games.

Adebawore recorded his fifth sack of the season early in the third quarter, when he took down C.J. Stroud for a seven-yard loss. Adebawore has already set a career-high in sacks through 11 regular-season games and has accumulated 31 tackles (15 solo), one defense and a scoop-and-score in 2026.

The rookie third-rounder recorded the first interception of his career in the first quarter, when a pass from C.J. Stroud intended for Nico Collins bounced off Haulcy's helmet, off the hands of Cam Bynum and into Haulcy's arms. The LSU product is up to 53 tackles (30 solo) and three pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.

It was a busy night for the rookie second-rounder, who finished with a career-high in stops while logging double-digit tackles for the third time this season. Allen has 45 total tackles over his last four outings, and most of that extra playing time has come in the absence of Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee, IR).

Watkins played just five offensive snaps for the Colts in Thursday night's game. Despite playing only 10 percent of the offensive snaps, Watkins totaled the third-highest yardage by Colts pass catchers on the night with his 26-yard grab. The reserve wide receiver could see an expanded role down the stretch as the Colts experiment with starting quarterback Anthony Richardson in what is all but a lost season.

Dulin played 22 offensive snaps and 10 special-teams snaps in the contest. The No. 4 wide receiver saw plenty of attention, catching 50 percent of his targets to accumulate the second-highest receiving yardage for the Colts, behind Anthony Gould's 48 yards.

Burks was the No. 2 wide receiver for the Colts in the contest. Despite being targeted three times, the wide receiver could not haul in any passes from since-cut quarterback Daniel Jones. Burks played 32 offensive snaps and two special-teams snaps in the contest.

Shrader opened Thursday's scoring with a 34-yard field goal early in the first quarter. Those ended up being the only three points scored by the Colts, as Shrader missed a 56-yarder later in the quarter, and his 62-yarder in the second quarter was blocked by Logan Hall. It was the second time this season that Shrader has missed two kicks, and the third-year kicker now is 24-for-28 on field-goal attempts (including 9-for-12 on kicks from 50-plus yards) and 19-for-20 on extra-point tries through 11 regular-season games. His scoring potential figures to be lower for the rest of the season after the Colts waived Daniel Jones on Friday, which paves the way for Anthony Richardson to start under center in Week 12 against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Thomas has had a disappointing third season in Jacksonville, mustering a meager 84 receiving yards over his last eight appearances while seemingly having fallen out of favor in coach Liam Coen's offense. Washington's absence against Tennessee's struggling secondary could provide Thomas with an opportunity to turn back the clock and turn in a performance reminiscent of the 2024 first-round pick's elite rookie season. Jakobi Meyers and Josh Cameron could also earn expanded roles in Jacksonville's wide-receiver room.

Cameron and Brian Thomas are the top candidates to absorb extra targets alongside Jakobi Meyers in Washington's absence. Washington is considered week-to-week, so his absence could extend beyond Week 12. Cameron has 111 receiving yards and a touchdown over the past two games, so the rookie sixth-round pick was trending up even prior to Washington's injury. An increased role against a Titans defense that's giving up the most catches and yards per game to wide receivers could set Cameron up for a breakout performance.

Meyers has managed to shake off an ankle injury that limited his practice participation earlier in the week. He racked up a season-high 85 yards on 10 targets in Jacksonville's Week 11 loss to the Giants, and Meyers is likely to get plenty of attention from Trevor Lawrence against Tennessee's league-worst secondary Sunday in the absence of top Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington (shoulder), giving Meyers appealing upside in nearly all fantasy formats.

Tuten was unable to practice this week, and will now target a potential return to action Dec. 6 against the Bears. In his absence this weekend, Chris Rodriguez will be in line for an increased workload in the Jacksonville backfield, a context that gives him Week 12 fantasy relevance, with LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah also in the mix versus 1-9 Tennessee.

Washington's shoulder injury seems to have taken a sudden turn for the worse, but the Jaguars had been preparing for their top receiver to be available, so they hadn't been utilizing Hunter much on offense in practice. Hunter should hold down his usual outside cornerback role on defense, but it's likely that most of the targets vacated by Washington will go to some combination of Jakobi Meyers (ankle), Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and CJ Williams rather than Hunter among Jacksonville's wide receivers.

Washington was added to Jacksonville's injury report Thursday due to a shoulder injury, and the impact of the injury has escalated from limiting his practice participation Thursday to sidelining Jacksonville's top receiver Sunday and possibly beyond then. In Washington's absence, Jakobi Meyers (ankle), Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and possibly Travis Hunter or CJ Williams -- to a lesser degree -- could garner more attention from Trevor Lawrence against a Titans secondary that has allowed the most catches and yards per game in the league to wide receivers. Additional details regarding Washington's injury should emerge before the Jaguars travel to Chicago in Week 13.

Striggow will be good to go for Sunday's matchup against the Titans after clearing the league's concussion protocol. The 24-year-old has compiled 13 tackles (nine solo), including 1.0 sacks, across nine games this season while playing on both defense and special teams.

Mekari now has a 21-day window for the Jaguars to return him to the active roster. The right guard returned to practice as a limited participant. If Mekari can upgrade to a full participant by Friday's session, there is a chance he could be activated for Sunday's game against the Titans. The Jaguars could just as easily take it slow with the veteran offensive lineman to ensure he is healthy and ready for his return to the field, so Ezra Cleveland may be in line for another start at right guard.

Jones suffered a chest injury during the first half of the Jaguars' 23-18 loss to the Giants in Week 12 and did not return. However, his full session Wednesday indicates that Jones' injury isn't a severe one and puts him on track to play in Sunday's AFC South tilt against the Titans. Jones has 26 tackles (19 solo) and eight pass defenses (including an interception) across 10 regular-season games.
questionable

Oluokun had a solid outing despite the loss, logging a team-high nine tackles while playing every defensive snap. The 2018 sixth-round pick has now totaled 77 tackles (48 solo), including 2.0 sacks, two interceptions and a forced fumble across 10 games this season.

Allen played 14 offensive snaps behind Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) and Chris Rodriguez, and Tuten ended up aggravating his ankle issue in the defeat. If Tuten needs to miss time, Allen could see elevated snaps behind Rodriguez, though Ameer Abdullah also is an option for the Jaguars out of the backfield. Ultimately, Allen is much likelier than not to remain irrelevant in fantasy.

For the first time since Week 3, Morris earned more playing time on offense than rookie Tanner Koziol (four snaps), who had previously been serving as the Jaguars' No. 3 tight end. Koziol offers more of a pass-catching threat at the position, but Morris is the superior blocker and also has a more integral role on special teams.

The rookie fifth-round pick saw his streak of three straight games with a reception come to an end and also had his snap count decline for the fourth week in a row. Koziol ranked fourth in playing time among Jacksonville tight ends, marking the first time since Week 3 that he had played behind Quintin Morris (11 snaps Sunday).

Though quarterback Trevor Lawrence dropped back a season-high 50 times on the day and targeted nine different players, Boerkircher wasn't able to earn a look in the passing game. The second-round rookie out of Texas A&M is regarded mainly as a run-blocking specialist, but he had carved out a minor role in the passing attack with at least one reception in each of Jacksonville's previous six contests.

Strange was able to notch at least three catches for the first time since Week 6, but he still finished with fewer than 20 receiving yards for the second straight week and third time overall this year. The tight end has now reeled in 35 of 43 targets for 381 yards and two touchdowns over 10 contests during the 2026 season.

After recording consecutive four-catch tallies following his trade from the Colts, Downs' production saw a downturn Thursday in a game where both air attacks performed below their usual levels. The talented receiver did make good use of his one reception, and Downs should be busier in a Week 13 road matchup against the Rams next Thursday night where weather shouldn't be a factor.

Since Josh Downs arrived via trade from Indianapolis at the deadline, Rashee Rice is leading all Chiefs wide receivers in targets with 17 over the last three contests, followed by Downs' 14, Worthy's 10, Cyrus Allen's nine, Jalen Royals' (ankle) two and Andrew Armstrong's two. Worthy's average number of targets has reduced from 5.9 per game pre-Downs to 3.3 since the addition to the position group, and the former has just a 2-38-1 line during that span. As a result, Worthy is difficult to trust as Kansas City prepares to face the Rams on the road next Thursday.

Rice's production was part of the collateral damage of a night that was unconducive for offense, as the veteran receiver tied his lowest reception and receiving yardage totals of the season for a non-injury-shortened game. Rice came in riding a solid four-game stretch where he'd generated a 23-237-1 line on 27 targets, and he'll look to return to that level of production during a Week 13 road matchup against the Rams next Thursday.

Smith was injured in the fourth quarter of Week 12 action, but the Chiefs never announced the reason for him hitting the sideline until Reid spoke to the media afterward. If the severity of Smith's issue is enough to require an absence or more time off, Hunter Nourzad is the likely candidate to man right guard for Kansas City.

Like Josh Allen, Mahomes didn't come close to putting up his typical caliber of production in the poor weather conditions Thursday, although the latter was at least relatively efficient compared to his opposite number. However, Mahomes failed to throw at least one touchdown pass for the first time in five games, and his yardage total was his second-lowest of the campaign. Mahomes will look to bounce back in what will be an appreciably better environment for offense during a Week 13 road matchup against the Rams next Thursday night.

Royals left the game in the third quarter and was ruled out not long afterward due to an ankle injury. The severity of the sprain will determine if Royals is in danger of missing any time. If that comes to pass for Royals, Andrew Armstrong likely will be on track for a few more offensive snaps behind Rashee Rice, Josh Downs, Xavier Worthy and Cyrus Allen.

Kelce, who shook off a hard hit to his lower back late in the first half, ended up posting a game-high receiving yardage total with the help of a game-long 24-yard grab that he made late in the first half, and he also tied for the team lead in receptions. The star tight end did have a couple of missed connections with Patrick Mahomes on fourth-quarter drives, however, plays that could have had an impact on the outcome of such a close game. Kelce has exceeded 65 receiving yards in four of the last five games heading into a Week 13 road showdown against the Rams next Thursday night.

Making a third straight start in place of Kenneth Walker (groin), Johnson put together another useful all-around performance that included his third rushing touchdown of the season on a one-yard run early in the third quarter. Johnson also recorded at least four catches for the third consecutive game, and he's now accumulated 410 scrimmage yards and four total TDs over his three starts. Walker is likely to be back for next Thursday's Week 13 road showdown against the Rams, but Johnson is likely to retain a solid complementary role even when his star teammate is back on the field.

Nussmeier has yet to appear in a game this season but will once again serve as the team's emergency quarterback. The rookie seventh-round pick will only be able to play against Buffalo if both Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

Woods drew the questionable tag for Thanksgiving Day, and the rookie first-rounder has been cleared by medical staff to return from a three-game absence due to a neck injury. In seven regular-season games prior to the injury, Woods accumulated 13 tackles (three solo), including 0.5 sacks, and one pass defense while operating in a rotational role on the Chiefs' interior defensive line.

Gray injured his ribs against the Cardinals on Sunday, and after logging full practices Tuesday and Wednesday, the sixth-year tight end has been cleared by medical staff to play on Thanksgiving Day. He has a 19-211-1 receiving line on 25 targets through 10 regular-season games while operating as the Chiefs' TE2 behind Travis Kelce.

FitzPatrick signed with the Chiefs' practice squad Nov. 17, and he'll now be available to make his 2026 regular-season debut to provide depth at tight end in the event that Noah Gray (ribs) cannot play Thursday. FitzPatrick appeared in 15 regular-season games for the Packers in 2025 and posted a 12-72-1 receiving line on 15 targets.

It's the third and final time Carter is eligible to be elevated from the practice squad, so he would need to be signed to the 53-man roster in order to suit up for the Chiefs beyond Week 12. With Kenneth Walker (groin) out for a third consecutive game, Carter will operate as Kansas City's RB3 behind Emmett Johnson and Jaydn Ott.

Despite logging full participation sessions in Week 12 prep, Norman-Lott will not suit up for Thursday night's contest. The Chiefs activated the defensive tackle from the reserve/PUP list Nov. 18, but he is not quite ready to return to the field.
Moore will miss his third consecutive game with an ankle injury. Joshua Ezeudu will once again be called upon to start at right tackle for the Chiefs' offense.

injuries.evidence: VanSumeren didn't practice Tuesday due to a sprained knee that will now keep him out for at least the next four weeks, according to Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site.
injuries.detail: VanSumeren didn't practice Tuesday due to a sprained knee that will now keep him out for at least the next four weeks, according to Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site. In six regular-season games in 2026, the fourth-year pro played a majority of his reps on special teams, with just six of 104 total snaps coming on offense.

Tranquill led the team in stops in Week 11, notching at least eight tackles for the third straight week. He was able to put together an impressive performance while playing a season-low 39 defensive snaps as a result of the team's blowout victory. Tranquill has now compiled 83 total tackles (42 solo), two passes defensed and a fumble recovery over the team's first 10 games of the 2026 campaign.

Bolton was on the field for a season-low 38 defensive snaps as Kansas City dominated the Cardinals in Week 11, and as a result, he notched his fewest takedowns since Week 1. The linebacker has now registered 94 total tackles (46 solo), three passes defensed and two forced fumbles over 10 contests to open the 2026 season.

Karlaftis was a man on a mission in Week 11, getting to Cardinals quarterback Josh Johnson on three separate occasions. The defensive lineman combined with teammate Chris Jones to sack Johnson in the second quarter before securing full sacks of the quarterback on back-to-back plays in the third quarter. Karlaftis is now up to 38 total tackles (20 solo), including 8.0 sacks, while also adding a career-high 10 passes defensed, one of which is an interception, and two forced fumbles over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

Allen was able to reel in multiple passes for the second straight week after having done so only twice in the team's first eight games of the year. The wide receiver played 16 offensive snaps which ranked sixth at his position behind Xavier Worthy (47), Rashee Rice (32), Jalen Royals (24), Andrew Armstrong (20) and Josh Downs (17). As a result of the depth of the WR room in Kansas City, Allen will remain a hard fantasy option to trust Thursday versus the Bills.

Ott logged 12 offensive snaps and eight special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The running back saw a few carries behind Emmett Johnson due to the absence of Kenneth Walker (groin). With Walker likely returning for Thursday night's game against the Bills, Ott may not see the field on offense in that contest.

Per Sam Warren of The Athletic, Bowers didn't practice on Friday after being limited the previous two days. It's unclear if the star TE's 'DNP' to close the week was maintenance or setback-related, but the Raiders' late kickoff presents an issue for those considering Bowers in Week 12 fantasy lineups. As one of the marquee names carrying a 'questionable' tag into the weekend, look for added context regarding his status to arrive no later than Saturday night or Sunday morning by via the usual notable NFL insiders.

Hemingway is still battling the shoulder injury that sidelined him for the Week 11 loss to Denver. The 25-year-old will likely need to be upgraded to a full participant in Friday's practice in order to avoid an injury designation for Sunday's matchup against the Browns.

Butler enterted the NFL's concussion protocol after being ruled out for the remainder of the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos. The defensive tackle will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to return to full-contact practice.

Pegues exited the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos late in the fourth quarter and did not return to the contest. The defensive tackle's full participation and injury clearance in the first prep session of Week 12 imply Pegues did not return to the Week 11 loss because he exited late, when the game was out of reach.

Johnson was a full participant in Wednesday's practice in what was his first on-field action since being placed on injured reserve in late October due to a neck injury. His ability to practice in full is an encouraging sign, but Johnson would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Browns.

Young was diagnosed with a stinger in the first half of the Raiders' 38-24 loss to the Broncos and did not return. However, his ability to practice in full Wednesday indicates that the fifth-year wide receiver will be available for Sunday's road game against the Browns. Young has mostly operated on special teams this season and has not been targeted in the passing game since Week 4 against the Chiefs.

Chinn was on the field for all 73 of the team's defensive snaps, and as a result, he was able to notch at least seven stops for the seventh straight game. The safety has now registered 79 total tackles (52 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding an interception, two forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries over 11 contests this season.

It was Walker's fourth game this season with double-digit tackles, and he's now up to 91 tackles (39 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a pair of fumble recoveries across 11 games this season. He's taken a bit of a back seat to Nakobe Dean in the tackles department for Las Vegas, as Dean leads the NFL with his 119 total tackles.

The linebacker has at least a dozen tackles in seven of 10 games this season and leads the NFL with 119 tackles (56 solo). He's also recorded three pass breakups, including one interception, three forced fumbles and a fumble recovery while playing 100 percent of the Raiders' defensive snaps.

Thomas had the opportunity to step into the TE2 role behind Michael Mayer on Sunday due to the absence of Brock Bowers (ankle/quadriceps). Thomas' 35 offensive snaps were his most of the season, and he made his lone target from Fernando Mendoza count, with the duo connecting on a 19-yard touchdown pass late in the third quarter to tie the game up at 17-17. Thomas has seven catches on as many targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns through 11 regular-season games, although he would revert to being the No. 3 tight end in Week 12 against the Browns on Nov. 29 if Bowers is cleared to return for that contest.

Gay has attempted only one field goal in three of his last four outings, and his lone try Sunday was a chip shot from 28 yards out. He's 22-for-24 on field-goal attempts through 11 regular-season games, and he's ranked fifth in the NFL in made field goals. The Raiders will hit the road for Week 12 against the Browns on Nov. 29.

Nailor caught one pass for the second straight week, and he has exceeded 20 receiving yards only one time since Week 1. The wide receiver was unable to capitalize on the absence of Brock Bowers (ankle) in Week 11, and Nailor figures to remain an unattractive fantasy option in Week 12 against the Browns.

Tucker finished with a team-high 10 targets, but he was unable to get on the same page with quarterback Fernando Mendoza for the majority of the game. Most of the wide receiver's production came on a 39-yard catch in the fourth quarter, and he has now combined to reel in three of 12 targets for 59 yards over Mendoza's first two career starts.

With only seven targets and four catches through 11 games to begin his career, Washington requires volume on the ground to produce, which is difficult to come by in a backfield led by Ashton Jeanty. And Jeanty was the engine of the Raiders offense Sunday, racking up 16 touches for 169 yards from scrimmage and one receiving TD. A rookie fourth-rounder, Washington is averaging just 3.9 yards per carry and has scored only one touchdown ahead of next Sunday's road matchup with the Browns.

Mayer missed out on a prime opportunity with top TE Brock Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) inactive in Week 11. When Bowers was out in Weeks 1 and 2 as he recovered from a meniscus trim in his left knee, Mayer went for a combined 9-55-0 line on 11 targets in those contests, but the latter also missed a stretch in the fourth quarter this Sunday due to a back injury. Bowers' status will be worth monitoring this week, as an absence from him next Sunday in Cleveland will set up Mayer for another key chance to produce.

After throwing for no touchdowns or interceptions in his first NFL start last Sunday against the Seahawks, Mendoza recorded the first scoring strike of his career on a 68-yard catch and run via RB Ashton Jeanty in Week 11. Mendoza also hooked up with Ian Thomas (19 yards) and Jack Bech (seven yards) for his other two TDs, but he followed up a 58.6 completion percentage in Week 10 with more misfires (19) than connections (18) this Sunday. Mendoza's next chance for game action is next Sunday at Cleveland.

Jeanty's 169 yards from scrimmage amounted to the second-highest single-game total of his career after going for 188 such yards against the Texans in Week 16 of last season. His performance was fueled by a 68-yard catch and run for a touchdown and a 46-yard rush, the latter of which marked his first of 20-plus yards on the campaign. Jeanty also broke a streak of four straight contests falling short of 10 carries, but considering No. 2 RB Mike Washington also earned nine runs in Week 11, the Raiders backfield remains a committee ahead of next Sunday's outing at Cleveland.

Bech finished second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Tre Tucker (10), and he was able to reel in a seven-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Fernando Mendoza in the fourth quarter. The score was Bech's first since Week 1, and his 88 receiving yards bested his previous season total of 67 yards entering Week 11. The wide receiver appears to have great chemistry with Mendoza, garnering 16 targets over the quarterback's first two career starts.

Keenan went down with a knee injury in the first half, and he will now officially be sidelined for the rest of Week 11. With Adam Butler (concussion) also done for the day, JJ Pegues will handle the bulk of the workload at defensive tackle versus the Broncos.

Thornton is dealing with a back injury, but he wasn't listed on Las Vegas' practice report during Week 11 prep. As such, it appears the second-year wideout is a healthy scratch Sunday. Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor, Jack Bech, Dareke Young and Cody White will make up the Raiders' WR corps.

Fatukasi was tagged as questionable due to a toe injury, although he ended Week 11 prep with a full practice Friday, and he's now been cleared by medical staff to play Sunday. The veteran defensive lineman has 16 tackles (four solo), including 1.0 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble through 10 regular-season games.

After Herbert missed practice Thursday and again wasn't spotted Friday, his status for Sunday's game against the Patriots appears to be trending in the wrong direction. If the Chargers' starting quarterback doesn't clear concussion protocol in time, DJ Uiagalelei would be in line to make the first regular-season start of the latter's NFL career against a Patriots team that's set to start backup QB Tommy DeVito.

Njoku also was deemed a 'DNP' on Wednesday, so the tight end presumably will need to practice Friday, in some capacity, in order to avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Patriots. If Njoku ends up sidelined this weekend, Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden will be in line to lead the Chargers' Week 12 TE corps.

injuries.detail: It's not clear when Leonard was injured, as he logged a season-high 70 percent defensive snap share against the Jets last Sunday. Regardless, he's now required to miss at least four games while on IR. Avery Smith and Isas Waxter may get more opportunities in the secondary during Leonard's absence.

Browning joined Los Angeles' practice squad Oct. 13 and had been there since before being promoted to the active roster Thursday. The move could be a bad sign for starting QB Justin Herbert, who is in concussion protocol and could  miss Sunday's clash against New England. Should Herbert miss that game, rookie DJ Uiagalelei would likely log his first NFL start, with Browning working as his backup.

The rookie first-rounder is working through an ankle injury that he picked up during the first half of the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the Jets in Week 12. Mesidor has two more opportunities to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's contest against the Patriots.

Tuipulotu appears to have sustained his ankle injury in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets. The outside linebacker will need to upgrade his practice participation in Thursday or Friday's session for a chance to suit up for Sunday's contest against the Patriots. If the 24-year-old must miss the game, Akheem Mesidor (ankle) or Caleb Murphy will likely start opposite Khalil Mack.

Thompson has not played since the Chargers' Week 2 game with the Raiders. The wide receiver initially dealt with a quadriceps injury before sustaining a hamstring injury while still recovering. Thompson's long string of DNPs continues into Week 12 prep, and it appears there may be no end in sight.

Tomlinson likely sustained his knee injury in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets. The defensive tackle will likely need to return to practice by Friday's session for a chance to suit up for Sunday's game against the Patriots.

Still did not play in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets due to an ankle injury he sustained in Friday's practice. The cornerback remains sidelined with the issue, leaving Deane Leonard and Genesis Smith as the early options at slot cornerback for Sunday's game against the Patriots.

Henley did not play in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets due to his knee injury. The linebacker has not practiced since sustaining the injury after Week 10. If Henley cannot suit up for Sunday's game, Marlowe Wax and Troy Dye will likely see increased snap shares at inside linebacker next to Del'Shawn Phillips.

The running back was injured in last Sunday's loss to the Jets. If Mitchell needs to miss time, it would likely turn this frustrating three-way committee backfield into a more traditional two-man affair, with Omarion Hampton handling early-down work and Kimani Vidal spelling him in passing situations.

Gadsden ranked third in snaps among Chargers tight ends, finishing only slightly behind Charlie Kolar (30) and David Njoku (25). Despite arguably being the most talented pass catcher of the trio, Gadsden was the only one of the three who failed to draw a target in Week 11. The 2025 fifth-round pick has endured a disappointing sophomore campaign, having thus far put together a 20-179-1 receiving line on 30 targets over 10 games while topping 40 receiving yards on just one occasion.

The safety has finished with five or more stops in seven of the eight games he's played in this season. Molden has 44 tackles (25 solo), a pass breakup and a fumble recovery in 2026.
The linebacker recorded at least four stops for the fourth game in a row and the ninth time in 10 games this season. Phillips has 53 tackles (23 solo) and an interception on the year.

Kolar was cleared to play Sunday after progressing through the league's concussion protocol, and his 30 offensive snaps were ahead of fellow tight ends David Njoku (25) and Oronde Gadsden (23). Kolar's eight-yard catch midway through the first quarter was the only pass that the fifth-year pro saw from Justin Herbert, but no Chargers pass catcher saw more than five targets other then Ladd McConkey (eight). Kolar has a 16-153-0 line on 24 targets through eight regular-season games heading into Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29.

Dicker's field goal was drilled from 52 yards, and he's now 19-for-21 on field-goal tries and 15-for-15 on extra points through 10 games this season. In a Chargers offense struggling mightily to score points, Dicker's fantasy value has tanked this season.

Johnston was targeted on just 9.5 percent of Justin Herbert's 21 pass attempts against New York. The wideout has now caught exactly one pass in three straight games and in five of his last six contests. Johnston is a lightly targeted deep threat who will likely continue to see fewer looks if Ladd McConkey is able to maintain his health for an extended period.

After handling just four touches last week against the Ravens, Vidal saw his usage increase again as he recorded his most scrimmage yards since Week 5. This time, however, his additional volume came at the expense of Keaton Mitchell (knee), who left the game early. Omarion Hampton has re-established himself as the Chargers' clear No. 1 RB over the last few contests, but if Mitchell's injury proves to be serious, Vidal could have some deeper-league appeal with the No. 2 role all to himself. He'll look to take advantage of whatever opportunities he gets in Week 12 against the Patriots.

With Ladd McConkey back in the lineup, Harris' role in the passing attack shrank after he'd turned 12 targets over the prior two games into an 8-92-0 line. Harris' fantasy appeal would collapse even further if Justin Herbert (concussion) ends up missing any time. The second-year wideout will at least get a promising matchup in Week 12 against a vulnerable Patriots secondary.

His longest gain went for just 11 yards, but McConkey was deadly in the red zone, connecting with Justin Herbert on scores of 11 and six yards in the fourth quarter as the Chargers tried to mount a late comeback. Herbert was placed in the concussion protocol after the game after taking six sacks, and if he end up missing any time, it would put a big damper on McConkey's fantasy outlook with undrafted rookie DJ Uiagalelei being the Bolts' backup, unless Trey Lance (groin) is able to return from IR. McConkey has had plenty of trouble staying on the field himself this year, of course, and he'll take a 22-323-3 line on 32 targets through seven contests into a Week 12 clash with the Patriots.

While he's still not seeing a consistent bell-cow workload, Hampton has turned his season around over the last three games, racking up 254 rushing yards and a TD while averaging 5.2 yards per carry. Keaton Mitchell left Sunday's game early with a knee injury, but his absence appeared to provide a bigger boost to Kimani Vidal, who wound up logging nine touches and 54 scrimmage yards. Hampton will look to keep rolling in Week 12 against the Patriots.

Pipkins had been on IR since late September before being activated Saturday. The veteran offensive lineman is now set to give the Chargers' offensive line a boost. Pipkins may work in a rotational role, as Logan Taylor is "locked in" at left guard, per Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com.
Waxter was cleared to return from a one-game absence due to an ankle injury. His availability gives the Chargers another contributor on special teams and depth in the secondary.

Allen was injured in the second quarter of Wednesday's win over the Packers. The Rams are still evaluating the extent of Allen's injury, but Rapoport mentions that high-ankle sprains are typically accompanied by recovery timelines of 4-to-6 weeks, so Allen is looking exceedingly unlikely to be available for the Rams' next game, Dec. 3 against the Chiefs.

Higbee and Davis Allen (ankle) were both injured during Wednesday's win over the Packers. Allen is likely facing a multi-week absence due to a high-ankle sprain, but Higbee still has a chance to avoid missing additional action. Colby Parkinson and Max Klare are the only healthy TE options remaining for the Rams.

McManus scored the first six points of the game with 43-yard and 41-yard field goals in the first quarter. He added a 40-yarder in the fourth and a 30-yarder just before the end of the game. The veteran kicker has yet to try a field goal from 50-plus yards, but he's been everything the Rams could have asked for since taking over as the team's kicker in Week 7. Through five games, McManus is a perfect 9-for-9 on FG attempts and 16-for-16 on PAT tries.

After posting a career-high 61 percent offensive snap share in Week 10 against Arizona, Daniels logged just a 22 percent share Wednesday. That was still good for third among Rams wideouts behind Konata Mumpfield (90 percent) and Xavier Smith (23 percent), but Daniels didn't get a pass thrown his way. If Davante Adams (hamstring) is able to return to action in Week 13 against the Chiefs on Thursday, Dec. 3, Daniels' prospects for making an impact in the passing game will likely fall even further.

Atwell logged just six offensive snaps, behind all of fellow wideouts Konata Mumpfield (70), Xavier Smith (18) and CJ Daniels (17). The Rams also gave more offensive snaps to four different tight ends. Atwell's usage is especially notable given that both Puka Nacua (IR, knee/toe) and Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) didn't play. Nacua is out for the season, but Adams could return as soon as Week 13 versus Kansas City. Atwell is not an advised fantasy play moving forward even if Adams has to miss more contests.

Smith was used as a ball carrier for the first time this season and gained a chunk of yards on each of his totes. Aside from that, it was another quiet game for the third-year wideout, who hasn't really been able to take advantage of a wide open WR pecking order in the wake of injuries to star wideouts Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring). In fact, Smith has logged less than a 25 percent offensive snap share over the past two games with the pair of stud WRs absent, so it appears head coach Sean McVay is looking elsewhere to fill the void. As such, Smith doesn't have much fantasy value given that his primary role is in the return game.

The Rams stuffed the ball down the throat of Green Bay's defense, especially late, and ended up with a combined 241 yards on 47 rushes. However, Rivers didn't get a single one of those totes or even a snap on offense. The veteran running back logged season highs with 15 carries and 81 yards against Arizona in Week 10, but all of that work came in garbage time. It appears Rivers isn't going to be a factor outside of his return duties while both Kyren Williams and Blake Corum are healthy.

Parkinson logged a hefty 83 percent offensive snap count, highest among Los Angeles tight ends. His two receptions also tied for the team lead among players at the position, but he couldn't do much with those catches, gaining just one yard on the first and losing two yards on the second. However, Parkinson could take on an even more important role moving forward, as Tyler Higbee (chest) and Davis Allen (ankle) both left Wednesday's win early and didn't return. If neither of those players is ready to suit up in Week 13 against Kansas City on Thursday, Dec. 3, Parkinson and untested rookie Max Klare would lead a tight-end corps that quarterback Matthew Stafford typically looks to often.

Murray limped to the locker room early in the fourth quarter and never returned. Head coach Sean McVay didn't mention Murray's status following the win, but it sounds like he may be dealing with a more-than-minor injury. That would further deplete a Los Angeles offensive line that has been without starting left guard Steve Avila (hamstring) since he was hurt Week 9.

Mumpfield set the pace in receiving yards for the Rams while also sharing the team lead in both receptions and targets. The 2025 seventh-round pick has now posted back-to-back productive games -- he had a 3-81-0 line in the Week 10 win over the Cardinals -- but Wednesday's performance could have been even more rewarding had an apparent two-yard touchdown grab just before the halfway point of the third quarter not been ruled incomplete on replay. Mumpfield should retain a solid No. 2 role even if Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) returns for a Week 13 home matchup against the Chiefs on Thursday, Dec. 3, and the former will retain his No. 1 standing if his star teammate remains sidelined.

Playing his second game without both Puka Nacua (IR, knee/toe) and Davante Adams (IR, hamstring), Stafford saw a notable downturn in his numbers and posted a new season low in passing yards. The veteran signal-caller also threw an interception for the fifth straight game, although his pick Wednesday didn't lead to any Packers points since Los Angeles intercepted Jordan Love just two plays later. Stafford also failed to throw a touchdown pass for only the second time this season, and the fact he also lost tight ends Tyler Higbee (chest) and Davis Allen (ankle) to in-game injuries didn't help his cause. On the positive side, there's an outside chance Stafford has Adams back in the fold for a Week 13 home showdown against the Chiefs on Thursday, Dec. 3.

Williams had already been losing ground to Blake Corum in recent weeks, but the latter's takeover of the ground attack may have been finalized Wednesday with his career-best 184-yard, one-touchdown effort. Williams logged his final three carries on the Rams' final drive, but Corum was in the clear lead role throughout the majority of the night. Williams did add his seventh rushing touchdown of the campaign on a seven-yard run early in the second quarter, and his backseat role may have been influenced in part by the turf toe injury he's been dealing with for the past month. Nonetheless, Williams could be destined for a true complementary role if McVay opts to center the ground game on Corum moving forward.

Corum's stock had already been trending firmly up in recent weeks, but Wednesday may ultimately go down as the day he formally took the reins of the ground attack from Kyren Williams. The 2024 third-round pick compiled a career-best rushing total while also becoming the first Rams running back to reach the 30-carry threshold in a game during the Sean McVay era that began in 2017. Corum has now logged double-digit carries in five consecutive games, and he capped off his night with productive runs of seven, nine and 29 yards on Los Angeles' game-sealing drive. Corum's fantasy value naturally skyrocketed with Wednesday's performance, and he'll look to build on the outstanding performance in a Week 13 home matchup against the Chiefs on Thursday, Dec. 3.

Kinchens put a helmet-to-helmet hit on Watson along the sideline. Watson was injured on the play but was able to the locker room conscious and under his own power. Jaylen McCollough is in the game in the secondary in Kinchens' place.

Wright continues to struggle rushing the ball this season, averaging just 1.6 yards per carry across 30 rush attempts. The 23-year-old will look to improve upon his performance during the Week 12 matchup versus the Jets.
Allen played 16 special-teams snaps in the contest. The running back did not log an offensive snap, leaving all the rushing work to Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright.

Bell saw 34 offensive snaps in Sunday's contest but was inefficient with his opportunities. The Dolphins continues to try to involve the third-round rookie, but he's been frequently out of sync with quarterbacks Malik Willis (IR, abdomen) and Kyle McCord.

Tolbert played just eight of the Dolphins' 55 offensive snaps in Week 11, and he drew just one target for the third time in his last five games. Miami will probably continue to lean primarily on Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell at wide receiver in a Week 12 matchup versus the Jets.

Carlson was signed to the Dolphins' practice squad this past Tuesday, two weeks after being released by the Saints. Washington's six targets were third on the team, trailing Caleb Douglas (10) and Greg Dulcich (seven) on a day when Kyle McCord attempted 33 passes. Metellus has accumulated 68 tackles (32 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and four pass defenses across 10 regular-season games.

Wilson had only one tackle Sunday, but it was an impactful one as he took down Brock Purdy for a seven-yard loss in the third quarter to force the 49ers to punt on the next play. In his five outings since the Vikings' Week 6 bye, Wilson has accumulated 32 tackles (20 solo), including 3.5 sacks.

Since being reinstated from injured reserve in Week 5, Yurosek has cleared 40 percent snap shares in five of the Vikings' ensuing six games. Reichard failed to get the Vikings on the board in the first quarter after his 55-yard field-goal attempt missed to the left. Reichard is 24-for-28 on field-goal attempts through 10 regular-season games, and each of those misses have come from 50-plus yards. The Vikings will be home in a controlled environment for three of their next four games, starting in Week 12 against the Falcons on Nov. 29.

Mason had one more carry and eight more rushing yards than Aaron Jones, but Jones' totals included an 11-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. They have worked in a near-even split when both veteran RBs have been healthy, but Mason hasn't scored since Week 1. Jones tied the game with an 11-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter, but the 49ers outscored the Vikings 21-3 in the second quarter, forcing Minnesota into a more pass-heavy approach. Jordan Mason led the team with 38 rushing yards on 11 carries. Jones and Mason should continue to split carries in Week 12 against the Falcons, with Jones offering greater upside as a pass catcher.

In his return from a one-game absence, Hockenson finished second on the team in receiving yards behind Justin Jefferson's 86. Cousins was under center for the Vikings in the 2023 regular season, when Hockenson set career highs with 95 catches for 960 yards. Hockenson hasn't surpassed 455 yards in a regular season since, though he's on pace to do so this year, with 41 catches for 383 yards and three touchdowns through nine appearances heading into a Week 12 home game against the Falcons.

Jennings made his return to action after missing two games with a calf injury. The 29-year-old reeled in a season-high three passes, while his six targets were also the most he's had in a game this year. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 40 receiving yards in contest, and Jennings hasn't scored a touchdown this season. His next chance to accomplish both feats will come in Week 12 versus the Falcons.

After throwing a pick-six among his three interceptions when he faced San Francisco's defense in his final game with the Raiders in Week 9, Cousins had another interception returned for a touchdown by the 49ers in the second quarter of Sunday's loss. The Vikings took a 28-10 deficit into the halftime locker room, and Cousins was unable to orchestrate a comeback before Minnesota waved the white flag and inserted Carson Wentz for its final drive. Cousins is still strengthening his grasp on the offense two games into his reunion with the Vikings ahead of a Week 12 visit from the Falcons, with whom Cousins spent the previous two seasons.

Jefferson has experienced an uptick in usage since the Vikings reacquired Kirk Cousins. The star WR has 16 catches for 160 yards on 22 targets in two games with Cousins, though Jefferson hasn't scored since Week 8. Jefferson fumbled at the end of a 25-yard catch in the third quarter, turning what would have been one of his best plays of the night into a lowlight. Another heavy dose of targets from Cousins likely awaits Jefferson in Week 12 against the Falcons.

Brosmer will operate as the team's No. 3 option at QB for the second straight week. He will only be eligible to enter the game if both starter Kirk Cousins and primary backup Carson Wentz are forced out of the contest.

Jones -- who was managing a shoulder injury during Week 11 prep -- was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. Jones figures to be limited to a rotational role on offense while serving as a contributor on special teams.

Van Ginkel's practice reps were limited Wednesday and Thursday while managing a quadriceps injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Packers. In Van Ginkel's four outings since the Vikings' Week 6 bye, he has accumulated 14 tackles (eight solo), including 4.5 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery.

Douglas had 178 yards and a touchdown in a career-best two-game stretch spanning Weeks 8 and 9, but he was limited to one catch for four yards in his most recent appearance, which QB Drake Maye (lower leg) left early. With Tommy DeVito under center in Week 12, Douglas will try to get back on track in New England's banged-up passing game coming out of a bye week.

Hollins has 23 catches for 293 yards and one touchdown in six appearances this season.

Schooler did not play in Week 10 against the Lions due to hamstring injury, and he missed the Patriots' four prior games while recovering from a back issue. Week 10 was the third time this season that Elliss posted double-digit stops, and he ended up co-leading the Patriots in tackles with safety Kevin Byard. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so their next game will take place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Rhamondre Stevenson was active despite dealing with a knee issue during the practice week, but the veteran back gained just four yards on six carries, and Kiner wound up leading the Patriots' backfield in both volume and yardage. New England gets a Week 11 bye, so Kiner's role and usage for a Week 12 clash with the Chargers likely won't become clear until the health of Stevenson and Maye come into focus after the break.

Fant would be in line to operate as the top TE for the Saints if he gets the green light to suit up against the team for which he played last season. Rookie third-round pick Oscar Delp would be the next man up if Fant joins Johnson on the sidelines.

With Johnson missing his first game of the campaign and Noah Fant (calf) questionable for Sunday's matchup, Oscar Delp is the sole healthy player at the position on the active roster.

McCoy was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice but seems to be trending toward making his return after missing the last two weeks due to a biceps injury. The 29-year-old should resume his role as the team's starting center during Sunday's matchup against the Bengals.

Stutsman found himself in the right place at the right time when a Caleb Williams pass was batted into the air late in the second quarter, but the Saints weren't able to capitalize after starting in Bears territory. He also logged nine total tackles for a second straight game. His role in Week 12 against the Bengals will likely depend heavily on the status of Pete Werner (hamstring).

The rookie third-round pick out of Georgia has handled a muted role at tight end behind Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant this season, compiling five receptions for 26 yards on five targets through nine appearances. Lance was unable to reel in a deep pass from quarterback Tyler Shough in the first quarter, and he didn't get another look the rest of the game. Lance will continue to primarily serve as a special-teams asset for New Orleans moving forward, making him an unattractive option for fantasy managers.

Donaldson recorded season highs in both catches and targets, and he finished third on the Saints in both of those categories behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele. Donaldson's 32 offensive snaps were tied with Travis Etienne for most among Saints running backs Sunday, although Etienne saw a heavier workload with 14 carries for 76 yards while Alvin Kamara, who played only eight offensive snaps, found the end zone on a one-yard touchdown pass from Tyler Shough in the second quarter. Losers of three of their last four games, the Saints will look to reverse their fortunes in Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29.

The Saints didn't have a scoring drive until the second quarter, when Smyth made his season-long, 56-yard field goal to cut the lead going into halftime, his first of two 50-plus-yard FGs in the game. The 25-year-old also continued his perfect PAT percentage for the season, making his singular attempt (5-for-5 in three games). His play on kickoffs stood out Sunday, committing two penalties for kicking the ball out of bounds and giving Chicago excellent field position.

The veteran running back played just eight of 72 offensive snaps, while both CJ Donaldson and Travis Etienne played 32 each with Audric Estime a healthy inactive. Kamara has touched the ball just seven times on 24 snaps over the past two weeks, but he's turned three of those touches into short touchdowns. The Saints' three-man backfield continues to be one to try and avoid when making fantasy lineup decisions. Kamara's proverbial gas tank is nearing empty, but the Saints continue to give him high-value touches near the goal line while refusing to play him outside of the red zone.

Vele continues to run virtually every route for New Orleans, and the seven grabs matched his season high from Week 1 against the Lions, while Vele's 76 yards are a new high-water mark for the receiver. It was notable that Jordyn Tyson ran just 22 routes on Tyler Shough's 51 dropbacks against Chicago. The Saints offense has become tough to predict on a week-to-week basis. Vele is more of a low-ceiling fantasy WR4/5 most weeks.

One week after logging 13 targets as Tyler Shough's top downfield option, Tyson all but disappeared as Chris Olave instead saw WR1-worthy volume. The Saints' aerial attack simply may not be able to support both wideouts in the same game, which would mark Tyson as a volatile, but high-ceiling, fantasy asset for the rest of the season. The rookie will try to bounce back in Week 12 against the Bengals.

The former Jaguar was the clear No. 1 option in the backfield for the Saints. Etienne will attempt to build on this performance in Week 12 against the Bengals.

Despite the high volume of attempts, Shough couldn't get much going through the air while dealing with a ferocious Chicago pass rush that sacked him six times, including one for a fourth-quarter safety by Montez Sweat.
