The second-year QB will likely need to be a lot more productive in Week 12 if the Saints are going to keep up with Joe Burrow and the Bengals.

One week after taking a back seat to rookie Jordyn Tyson, Olave re-emerged as Tyler Shough's favorite downfield option, as he set a new season high in targets and topped 100 receiving yards for the fourth time in 2026. Tyson, meanwhile, caught only one pass on two targets, suggesting the Saints' aerial attack may not be able to support both wideouts in the same game. Olave will look to make an impact again in Week 12 against the Bengals.

As the emergency QB3, Wilson is not allowed to play Sunday unless starter Tyler Shough and backup Spencer Rattler both leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection. Wilson has yet to appear in a regular-season game in 2026.

Estime's role in the offense was reduced in Week 10 against the Panthers, which marked Travis Etienne's return from a five-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Estime is a healthy scratch for Sunday's game, which means Alvin Kamara and CJ Donaldson will operate as the rotational options out of the backfield behind Etienne. Estime's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29.
out

Likely was listed as limited on the injury report Wednesday and Thursday due to the groin strain that he picked up in practice last Friday, but it won't keep him from suiting up again in Week 12. While playing through the issue this past Sunday against the Jaguars, he took on a normal 76 percent snap share but recorded just one catch (on three targets) for 35 yards.

Carter was a DNP for Wednesday's session due to a calf issue, and the second-year edge rusher is now battling through an illness. His lack of practice reps are concerning, but he has one more opportunity to log at least a limited session ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts. Trace Ford and Dawuane Smoot would both be in line for more defensive snaps in the event that Carter is not cleared to play against Indianapolis.

The second-quarter reception was the first of the season for Manhertz, who had suited up for each of the Giants' previous nine games but was targeted just once. While taking the field for 19 of the Giants' 70 offensive snaps, Manhertz finished a distant second to Isaiah Likely (53 snaps) among the team's tight ends. Manhertz is expected to operate mostly as a blocker on offense while being a mainstay on the Giants' special-teams units.

Banks matched his season high in tackles while and was able to secure his second interception of the season, jumping in front of a short pass from Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence in the first quarter. The cornerback has now registered 33 total tackles (21 solo) and a career-high 14 passes defensed, including two interceptions, while also scoring a defensive touchdown over eight contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

Smoot was elevated from the practice squad to the active roster for three consecutive weeks between Weeks 9 and 11, and he accumulated three tackles (one solo), including 1.0 sacks, in that span. Now that he's on the active roster, Smoot will be available for the Giants for the rest of the season while serving in a rotational role at the edge rusher position behind Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux.

injuries.detail: Newsome is expected to undergo surgery for a sprained ankle that he sustained in the Giants' 23-18 win over the Jaguars on Sunday. Now that he's on IR, Newsome will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 16 against the Lions on Monday, Dec. 28. Paulson Adebo is expected to start opposite Deonte Banks at outside cornerback in Newsome's absence.

With Tremaine Edmunds (chest) done for the season, McFadden has started each of the last four games as an every-down linebacker. During that span, he's piled up 36 tackles (23 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and a fumble recovery.
The running back played just 10 offensive snaps behind starter Cam Skattebo. Singletary has averaged just 2.9 yards per carry this year on 41 attempts.

Quarterback J.J. McCarthy was inefficient against a solid Jaguars defense in Week 11, completing just 18 of his 38 pass attempts for 173 yards. A couple of those 20 incompletions were intended for an open Mooney, who continued to operate in the deeper areas of the field. He'll keep hunting for a big play in Week 12 at Indianapolis.

Johnson was third in offensive snaps (14) among Giants tight ends Sunday behind starter Isaiah Likely (49) and veteran Chris Manhertz (19). With that said, Johnson did manage to record at least one catch for the fourth time in his last five games. As long as Likely remains available, though, Johnson will remain in a rotational role.

Fields played 56 offensive snaps in the contest, logging 86 percent of the Giants' such plays. Despite the lack of catches, the No. 2 wide receiver continues to receive attention from quarterback J.J. McCarthy on a week-to-week basis.

The rookie kicker continues to have his ups and downs. While he was good from 53, 54 and 43 yards, Zvada missed a chip shot from 32 yards on the opening drive of the second half that left coach John Harbaugh shaking his head. Zvada continues to be a bit of a liability, as he's made just 11 of 18 field-goal attempts over his last six games. Harbaugh is clearly growing more frustrated by the week, and it could lead to the Giants making a move at the position.

McCarthy had his share of trouble against an aggressive Jaguars defense, leading to a season-worst 47.4 percent completion rate. However, the emerging signal-caller avoided turnovers and connected with Malik Nabers for an eight-yard touchdown pass in the second quarter. McCarthy also provided some timely contributions with his legs, and he's averaging 5.4 yards on his 22 rush attempts to date. McCarthy connected with nine different targets overall as he continues to show good command of the offense, and he'll look to bounce back efficiency-wise in a Week 12 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

Skattebo was unsurprisingly stymied on the ground by the Jaguars' elite run defense, and he couldn't really make up for it with his work through the air. Skattebo also committed another untimely turnover, fumbling at Jacksonville's 31-yard line with just over four minutes remaining in the third quarter and New York trying to add to a 20-6 lead. The change of possession ultimately didn't lead to any Jaguars points, however, and head coach John Harbaugh showed some faith in the second-year back by affording him the opportunity to ice the upset win with three carries on the final drive. Skattebo proved up to the task by netting 13 yards on those touches to force the Jags to exhaust their timeouts, and he should continue helming the backfield in a Week 12 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

Nabers was in the familiar position of leading the Giants across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and the third-year star also snapped a four-game touchdown drought with an eight-yard grab in the second quarter. Nabers has at least five catches in eight straight contests and three double-digit target tallies within that span, and the 2024 first-round pick should continue to be the subject of plenty of J.J. McCarthy's attention in a Week 12 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

Cooper will miss a second consecutive game Sunday, bringing him up to six total absences as a result of ankle injuries during his rookie campaign. Adonai Mitchell is set to start on the outside opposite Garrett Wilson, with Isaiah Williams manning the slot, though another elevation for practice-squad WR Sterling Shepard could be on the table after Shepard scored twice in the Week 11 win over the Chargers. Cooper's next chance to play will be a Week 14 home game against the Broncos following the Jets' Week 13 bye. Glenn said the timing of the bye played into the decision to keep Cooper out Sunday, per Rich Cimini of ESPN.com, which suggests Cooper has a decent chance to return after the bye.

Phillips upgraded to limited participation after sitting out Wednesday's practice, and he also managed to play through the ankle injury during the Week 11 win over the Chargers. Jack Heflin would be in line for increased playing time during Sunday's matchup against the Dolphins if Phillips ends up being unable to play.

Williams -- who was inactive in Week 11-- was listed as a limited participant on Wednesday's estimated practice report, but his full participation a day later paves the way for him to return to action Sunday against the Dolphins. With fellow wideout Omar Cooper (ankle/groin) in danger of missing his second straight game, Williams could end up working as the Jets' WR3 this weekend behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell in the event that he's active and Cooper isn't.

Onyemata was designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 18 but was not cleared to play against the Chargers in Week 11. If he can string together full practices over the next two days, then Onyemata would have a good chance of being activated from IR ahead of Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Dolphins.

Wallace missed the Jets' last three games due to a groin injury, but his absence from Wednesday's report indicates that he is fully healthy and will return for Week 12 against the Dolphins on Sunday. Wallace has mostly played on special teams in 2026 and has four assisted tackles and a fumble recovery across six regular-season games.
The defensive lineman was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. Sweat hasn't played since Week 7 and has logged 17 tackles (five solo) across 229 defensive snaps this season.

Since recording eight catches for 48 yards and a touchdown over the Jets' first three games, Ruckert has yet to draw a target in any of the team's subsequent eight contests. Ruckert's downturn in involvement in the passing game coincides with the Jets' top two tight ends -- Mason Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq -- getting back to full health after they were either limited or sidelined in the early part of the season.

The 30-year-old Beck has been one of the more versatile players in the league this season. In addition to taking snaps as a fullback and tight end, Beck often serves as a short-kickoff specialist for the Jets, while also contributing on the special teams coverage and return units. While the variety of roles he handles makes him valuable from a real-life standpoint, Beck maintains little fantasy relevance. He's carried twice for one yard and has yet to draw a target through the Jets' first 11 games.

It was the second consecutive week in which Davis posted six stops, and he finished Sunday's game tied for the second-most tackles on the Jets behind Jamien Sherwood (11). Davis is up to 74 total tackles through 11 regular-season games, and the 2012 third-rounder is well on pace to record his 10th-straight 100-tackle season.

Belton played every single defensive snap Sunday and finished tied for the second-most tackles on the Jets behind Jamien Sherwood (11). Belton has recorded at least six stop in 10 of 11 regular-season games and is up to 88 tackles (42 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and five pass defenses. He is well on his way to cracking the tackling century mark for a second consecutive season.

Week 11 was the third multi-sack performance of the season for Bailey, and his first takedown of Justin Herbert early in the second quarter resulted in a fumble that the Chargers recovered. Bailey is up to 9.5 sacks through 10 regular-season games, which leads all  rookies and is tied for third-most in the NFL behind Will Anderson (11.5) and Greg Rousseau (10.0). Bailey also leads the league with six forced fumbles, and the Texas Tech product is living up to his pedigree as the second-overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft.

It was the linebacker's fourth game this season with double-digit tackles. He also had a fourth-quarter sack wiped off the board by a Jets penalty. Through 11 games this season, Sherwood has recorded 97 tackles (49 solo), four pass breakups, three forced fumbles and a fumble recovery on 97 percent of the defensive snaps.

Shepard was elevated for Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers due to the absences of fellow wideouts Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs). The veteran receiver answered the call by hauling in both of his targets for 24 yards and two touchdowns in the win. Since Shepard has now been elevated the maximum three times, he'll need to be signed to the 53-man roster in order to suit up again for the Jets this season.

Sanders got the scoring started with a 50-yard field goal to cap the opening drive of the game. He later made one from 24 yards in the third quarter. Sanders has been a bright spot for the Jets this season, as he entered play Sunday leading the league in field-goal attempts (28) and makes (25), and he further boosted his conversion rate. The Jets have struggled to turn red-zone possessions into touchdowns this season, making Sanders a valuable fantasy kicker.

The Jets controlled this game from start to finish and never trailed, so Geno Smith attempted just 21 passes to 37 run plays for New York. Taylor's 25 yards were his most in a game since Week 7, and he's totaled just 10 catches for 75 yards and no touchdowns over his last four contests. He's a very risky play as a fantasy tight end.
As has been the case for three straight weeks, with Breece Hall back healthy, Davis has been glued to special teams for the Jets. He has no fantasy appeal.

Sadiq finished tied for second on the team in targets with wide receiver Adonai Mitchell and running back Breece Hall behind wideout Garrett Wilson (five). The tight end was able to reel in multiple passes for just the second time since catching seven of eight targets for 105 yards and a score in Week 3 against the Lions. Sadiq has now caught 25 of 36 targets for 268 yards and a score while adding a three-yard rushing touchdown over the first 11 regular-season contests of his career.

Even with Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) inactive, Mitchell's role didn't change, as his three targets tied with two other teammates for second on the team behind Garrett Wilson's five on a day the Jets called 37 run plays to just 22 passes. Mitchell has just one touchdown this season and has only 14 catches for 212 yards and no touchdowns in six games surrounding his 7-142-1 receiving performance from Week 8 against the Raiders. He's a big-play specialist in an offense that prefers to feed Wilson and its running backs.

Allen's 16 carries matched his total from the previous two games combined, as he had seen a downtick in opportunities since fellow RB Breece Hall returned from a quadriceps injury. Hall led the backfield once again with 100 scrimmage yards and a touchdown on 23 touches, but Allen was a key part of the game plan as well in the run-heavy win. The Jets will face a one-win team for a second consecutive game in Week 12 at Miami, which could allow Allen to stay involved alongside Hall.

Smith didn't have a completion longer than 21 yards but kept the offense on schedule with an accurate performance. Most importantly, he stepped up in the red zone, which has been the team's Achilles' heel throughout the season. Smith threw a seven-yard touchdown pass to Breece Hall to snap the Jets' two-game touchdown drought in the second quarter, then tacked on touchdown passes of eight and 15 yards to practice-squad elevation Sterling Shepard. The veteran QB will take a 15:3 TD:INT into a Week 12 road game against the Dolphins, who defeated the Jets in Week 7 despite three touchdown passes from Smith.

Cooper had a quiet outing despite the win, finishing fourth on the team in both receiving yards and receptions. Across 10 games this season, the 25-year-old has caught 17 passes for 259 yards and four touchdowns, all of which serve as new career highs.

Smith put together a career stat line during the Eagles' Thanksgiving Day win, with the veteran wide receiver hauling in 11 of 14 targets for 200 yards and two touchdowns. He was in and out of the game after landing hard on his tailbone on one of his targets in the fourth quarter and was in noticeable pain when on the field. Smith will have additional time to rest courtesy of the Thursday game, but his status over the coming days will be worth monitoring ahead of the Eagles' Week 13 road tilt against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Elliott had a strong outing in the victory, as he nailed the game-winning field goal from 59 yards out with two seconds left in the game. The 31-year-old has now converted 13 of his 14 field-goal attempts and all 21 of his extra-point tries across 11 games this season.

Goedert injured his right shoulder during the first half of Thursday's game and was not cleared to return. He'll undergo further tests to determine the severity of the injury, but the veteran tight end is certainly in jeopardy of not being available for the Eagles' Week 13 road tilt against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6. Johnny Mundt, Zach Ertz and rookie second-rounder Eli Stowers would all be in line for larger roles on offense if Goedert were to miss time.

The Eagles were down 28-10 at the half and watched Saquon Barkley (neck) and Dallas Goedert (shoulder) exit early, leaving Joe Milton with limited tools at his disposal to put together a comeback. DeVonta Smith saw most of the target volume, but Lemon came up big when it counted, connecting with Milton on a 24-yard TD that brought Philly to within two points with about two minutes left. While a two-point conversion attempt to tie the game failed, the stage was set for a game-winning 59-yard field goal by Jake Elliott in the dying seconds. Lemon has topped 50 yards in four of the last five games, producing a 25-249-2 line on 35 targets over that stretch, and the rookie's role could continue to grow in Week 13 against the Cardinals.

Saquon Barkley (neck) exited the game early with a stinger, leaving the backfield in the hands of Shipley. The Eagles had to abandon the run game after halftime, however, limiting his usage as Joe Milton engineered an incredible comeback with his arm and legs. Barkley spent most of his time on the sideline trying to talk the coaching and training staffs into letting him back on the field, suggesting his absence was just precautionary, but if he misses additional action, Shipley could be in line for a much bigger workload in Week 13 against the Cardinals.

Facing the team who put him on the practice squad to begin the season before he got signed by the Eagles, Milton used his mobility to keep plays alive and find receivers deep against an inept Cowboys secondary. The 26-year-old QB connected with DeVonta Smith for TDs of 50 yards in the second quarter and 45 yards in the third, before a big fourth quarter in which Milton ran in a 15-yard score of his own and then found Makai Lemon for a 15-yard strike as Philly erased a 38-24 deficit. Milton's 331 passing yards weren't just a career high, they were more than he produced in his first two starts this season combined. He'll remain under center against another struggling defense as he faces the Cardinals in Week 13.
Hall exited the game in the second half, casting doubt on his availability for the remainder of the contest. Ty Robinson could see an uptick in playing time if Hall ends up being unable to return.
Epps is done for the day after suffering a foot injury in the third quarter. In his absence, Kenny Moore has taken over at safety.

This marks Barkley's second diagnosed stinger of the campaign, but on the previous occasion in Week 2 against the Titans, he was able to check back in to the contest. The Eagles may opt to exercise caution with Barkley, however, because he tended to a neck issue on a short week following this past Sunday's win against the Steelers.

DeJean was shaken up on the Eagles' first defensive drive of the first quarter and was taken to the locker room, where medical staff diagnosed the third-year defensive back with a concussion. Michael Carter should see more defensive snaps in the secondary in the absence of DeJean, who will now work through the league's protocol in an effort to be available for Week 13 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6.
Payton will only take the field in Week 12 if starter Joe Milton and backup Tanner McKee leave the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

Mondon ended Week 12 prep with back-to-back limited practices, and that was enough for the second-year linebacker to avoid an injury tag ahead of Thanksgiving Day. He's mostly operated on special teams but served in a rotational role on defense in Week 9 against the Giants, and he finished that contest with a season-high five tackles (two solo).

After his trade to the Bengals fell through two weeks ago, Ebiketie is now dealing with an injury that will sideline him for at least one contest. Jalyx Hunt and A.J. Epenesa should soak up extra snaps off the edge for the Eagles.

The cornerback was injured in last Sunday's win over the Steelers. With Jones set to miss Thanksgiving Day against Dallas, Riq Woolen and Kelee Ringo are likely to see increased snaps opposite Quinyon Mitchell.

The star cornerback was injured in last Sunday's win over the Steelers, but the couple days of rest was enough for him to be available for Thanksgiving Day in Dallas. Mitchell has started all 10 games this season, producing 41 tackles (32 solo) and 11 pass breakups, including his first career interception. He should see plenty of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on Thursday.

McKee was estimated to be a limited participant on Monday's injury report due to an injury to his ribs. He now looks to be all set to serve as the team's primary reserve option at quarterback behind starter Joe Milton on Thursday against the Cowboys.

Young had a productive outing in the victory, logging his first two sacks of the campaign. The 26-year-old will look to build on this strong performance and keep producing during the Week 12 matchup against the Cowboys.

Trotter had a strong outing in the win, leading the team in tackles while playing every defensive snap. The 23-year-old has now tallied double-digit tackles in three straight games and will look to keep producing during Thursday's matchup versus the Cowboys.

The loose ball was recovered by the Steelers, and Pittsburgh's offense turned that takeaway into a 40-yard field goal by Chris Boswell four plays later. It ended up being the only touch of the game for Blue, who played all 11 of his snaps on special teams. There's an outside chance he sees some involvement on offense against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving Day, but that will depend on the availability of both Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) and Will Shipley (foot/illness).

Dallas Goedert (47 snaps), Johnny Mundt (eight) and Zach Ertz (six) handled tight-end duties for Philly, while Stowers played 20 snaps on special teams. The rookie tight end is miles from fantasy relevance this season.

Holcomb will sit out Friday's game after popping up on Thursday's injury report with a heel injury. His next chance to suit up will come Dec. 6 against the Texans. Carson Bruener and Jacoby Windmon could get more run as rotational inside linebackers in Holcomb's absence.

With Wetjen scratched, Max Hurleman is next in line to return kickoffs and punts on special teams. Hurleman is one of five active wide receiver for the Steelers on Friday, joining DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman, Germie Bernard and Roman Wilson.

Mason Rudolph will make his first start of the season Friday after the Steelers parted ways with Aaron Rodgers, while Howard moves up to the second spot on the team's quarterback depth chart. Drew Allar (coach's decision) will be Pittsburgh's emergency third QB behind Rudolph and Howard for Friday's game against the Broncos.

Following Aaron Rodgers' departure from Pittsburgh, Allar moves up to the third spot on the depth chart behind Friday's starter Mason Rudolph and Will Howard. Despite the incremental progress, it would take injuries or ejections for both Rudolph and Howard for Allar to get into Week 12 game action.

Herbig is set to make his return after missing the Week 11 loss to the Eagles due to a hip injury. The 2023 fourth-round pick will likely start at outside linebacker alongside T.J. Watt against the Broncos, as Alex Highsmith has been ruled out with an ankle injury.

Dunker managed to return to practice for the first time since suffering a knee injury in September but will have to wait at least another week before making his return. The rookie sixth-round pick should provide additional depth at guard once healthy.

Elliott was listed as a full practice participant Thursday, and that was enough for him to avoid an injury tag ahead of Friday's contest. The veteran defensive back has mostly operated in a rotational role in the secondary and has two solo tackles across three regular-season games.

Highsmith was held out of practice all week due to an ankle injury that he picked up during the Steelers' 19-16 loss to the Eagles this past Sunday, when he logged 2.0 sacks and forced a fumble before his exit. Nick Herbig and Jack Sawyer are the top candidates to start opposite T.J. Watt at the edge rusher position in the absence of Highsmith, whose next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Texans on Sunday, Dec. 6.

injuries.detail: Skowronek has been working through a calf issue since mid-October, and he appeared to aggravate the injury during the Steelers' Week 11 loss to the Eagles. Now that he's on injured reserve, Skowronek will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 16 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 27. Max Hurleman was signed off the practice squad to the 53-man roster in a corresponding move.

The move corresponds with the Steelers placing Ben Skowronek (calf) on injured reserve. Hurleman was called up from the practice squad and made his NFL regular-season debut against the Eagles in Week 11, when he caught six of seven targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in a 19-16 loss for the Steelers. He also returned three punts for 36 yards and two kickoffs for 32 yards, and with Skowronek on IR, Hurleman figures to take on more return duties moving forward. His production in his NFL debut came after DK Metcalf was ejected from the game, and with Michael Pittman (foot) activated from IR, Hurleman figures to be limited to a return role for Friday's contest against the Broncos.

Pittman last played in Week 4 but is slated to be back in the lineup versus Denver after logging 'full' practice listings Tuesday through Thursday. In his return, Pittman will bolster a Pittsburgh WR corps that also features DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard and Roman Wilson, with the veteran pass catcher's Week 12 fantasy upside hinging on how well he connects with newly-installed starting QB Mason Rudolph. Prior to his absence, Pittman recorded a 7-89-0 line on 12 targets through three contests.

Late Tuesday, the Steelers opted to make a change under center, naming Rudolph the Week 12 starter and sending Rodgers to the bench on the heels of poor performances by the offense in back-to-back losses to the Bengals and Eagles coming out of a bye week. The Steelers initially planned to make Rodgers inactive for Week 12 but keep him on the roster, but the team now intends to part ways with the four-time MVP after he harshly criticized head coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday. The impending departure of Rodgers should thus give Rudolph an extended leash as the Steelers' starter, with a pair of inexperienced quarterbacks in second-year man Will Howard and rookie third-round pick Drew Allar representing the other options behind him on the depth chart. Over 38 career appearances (19 starts), the 31-year-old Rudolph has completed 64.2 percent of his passes for 6.6 yards per attempt and a 30:22 TD:INT.

Ramsey matched his season low in takedowns, but he was able to notch his first pass defensed since Week 5. The 32-year-old will have a chance to bounce back on a short week, taking on the Broncos on Friday at home.

Queen entered Week 11 having notched double-digit tackles in three straight games, but his streak was snapped versus Philadelphia. The linebacker has now compiled 78 total tackles (28 solo), including 3.5 sacks, four passes defensed, one of which is an interception, and a forced fumble over 10 contests so far during the 2026 season.

One week after piling up 19 tackles (nine solo) in a loss to the Bengals, Wilson's three tackles Sunday were his fewest in a game this season. His 83 percent snap share on defense was also his lowest since Week 4. Wilson will be in position to rebound against Denver on Friday. He has 91 tackles (46 solo), including 1.0 sacks, four pass breakups, including an interception, and a fumble recovery across 10 games this season.

It was Wilson's first game since suffering a finger injury in Week 5 that landed him on injured reserve. He ended up playing 49 of 71 offensive snaps, 39 of which came out wide. Wilson had primarily operated as the Steelers' slot receiver prior to his injury, but Germie Bernard has emerged in that role for Pittsburgh. While Michael Pittman (foot) is expected back for Friday's game against the Broncos, DK Metcalf might receive some form of team-imposed discipline after he had an on-field meltdown against the Eagles before being ejected from the game.

With Michael Pittman (foot) remaining sidelined for Week 11, Bernard retained his every-down role on offense, playing 67 of 71 offensive snaps while leading the team in routes (52) and targets. It was a nice bounce-back game for the rookie after he was held without a catch on three targets against the Bengals in Week 10. Pittman is expected back for Friday's game against the Broncos, but Bernard could keep pacing the team in playing time, especially if DK Metcalf gets disciplined for his latest on-field outburst.

Metcalf was disqualified with 4:53 remaining in the third quarter Sunday after he attempted to poke Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean in the eye. He was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct in what was his second major transgression of the game; Metcalf previously drew an unnecessary roughness penalty in the first half, when he held his block of DeJean well after a play had finished. Though Metcalf won't miss further game action as a result of his ejection, he may have already lost the faith of his fantasy managers heading into a Week 12 matchup with the Broncos on Friday. Metcalf has hauled in just 36 of his 74 targets (48.6 percent catch rate) and has scored just two touchdowns on the season while topping 60 receiving yards in only two of his 10 appearances.

This was a battle of Pennsylvania's kickers, as Boswell and Jake Elliott combined to account for 23 of the game's 35 points. Boswell was good from 25, 40 and 52 yards. The veteran kicker has been trending downward the last two seasons, and he entered play Sunday having made just 79.2 percent of his field-goal tries this season. After his perfect showing against the Eagles, Boswell has made all of his field goals in back-to-back games for the first time all season. On the year, he's 22-for-27 on FGAs and a perfect 18-for-18 on PATs.

The big tight end earned just a 6.8 percent target share on a day when Aaron Rodgers fired off 44 pass attempts in prolonged comeback mode. Washington has been held to 25 yards or fewer in eight of 10 games this season. He doesn't see enough volume to warrant weekly fantasy consideration as a touchdown-or-bust bet.

Freiermuth matched his season high in catches, securing five passes in a game for the third time this year. The tight end has yet to exceed 50 receiving yards in a contest this season, and he entered Week 11 with exactly two catches in each of the team's last four games. Freiermuth has now caught 32 of 43 targets for 309 yards and five touchdowns while also adding four rushes for five yards and a score over 10 contests so far during the 2026 season.

Purdy appears poised to be listed as a non-participant for a third consecutive day during Week 12 prep as he tends to an ankle injury. Head coach Kyle Shanahan has yet to speak on Purdy's health concern, but Friday's practice report will reveal if the quarterback is in danger of missing Sunday's game against the Seahawks.

The 49ers didn't hold a practice for Thanksgiving Day, but Watkins has been listed as a non-participant for the first two sessions of Week 12 prep due to a groin injury. He has one more opportunity to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's game against the Seahawks. In the event that Watkins is not cleared to play against Seattle, more offensive snaps would be available for the likes of Jacob Cowing, Keenan Allen and Demarcus Robinson.

After not practicing Wednesday, Evans' upgrade in listing one day later generally is a good sign that he has a chance to suit up Sunday versus the Seahawks. In his return from a three-game absence this past Sunday against the Vikings in Mexico City, he logged just 43 percent of the snaps but reeled off six catches (on seven targets) for 109 yards and one touchdown.

Pleasants opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a knee injury that he sustained in a preseason game against the Chargers in late August. He was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, and he would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Seahawks. With Colton McKivitz (ankle) out for the rest of the season, Pleasants would be a candidate to start at right tackle once he's removed from IR.

injuries.evidence: He's expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season, and Vederian Lowe is expected to take over as the starter at right tackle in McKivitz's absence.
injuries.detail: McKivitz was diagnosed with a fractured and dislocated ankle that he sustained in the 49ers' Week 11 win over the Vikings. He's expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season, and Vederian Lowe is expected to take over as the starter at right tackle in McKivitz's absence.

Lenoir has been playing through a foot injury since Week 9 against the Raiders, so it's not surprising to see his practice reps limited Wednesday. Unless he suffers a setback, Lenoir should be available for Sunday's NFC West tilt against the Seahawks.

Greenlaw was not cleared by medical staff to play against the Vikings in Week 11 due to a neck issue. He's opened Week 12 prep with a limited practice, and a full session over the next two days would likely be enough for him to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Seahawks.

Okuayinonu suffered a broken foot in practice ahead of Week 1 and required surgery. He appears to be making progress and could return at some point before the end of the regular season. The 28-year-old appeared in 15 regular-season games last season, and made 12 starts and recorded 23 tackles (16 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and a forced fumble.
San Francisco needed to make a decision on Hobbs after his 21-day practice window was set to close. The veteran cornerback will be looking to make his 2026 debut Sunday against the Seahawks.

Stribling was diagnosed with a deltoid sprain of his left ankle after getting injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia and underwent surgery Sept. 16. The 23-year-old was handed an estimated recovery timeline of about 10 weeks, leaving the 49ers optimistic that he would be ready to play at some point in December. While Shanahan indicated that Stribling's timeline doesn't appear to have changed, the young wideout will need to get back on the practice field before the 49ers can hone in on a more precise target date for him to resume playing. Given the haziness of his return date along with the fact that he could face limitations with his snaps once activated, Stribling likely isn't worth holding in redraft leagues at this point in the season.

Willis has suited up in each of the 49ers' last nine games but has received little run on offense while the team's top two tight ends -- George Kittle and Luke Farrell -- have remained healthy throughout the season. The 27-year-old has logged single-digit snaps on offense in five straight contests and has yet to draw a target in 2026.

Farrell has suited up in each of the 49ers' first 10 games, but despite logging double-digit snaps in each contest, he's produced just four catches for 40 yards on seven targets. He'll continue to serve mainly as a blocking tight end on offense while also serving as a key contributor on the 49ers' special-teams units.

Brown picked off a pass from Kirk Cousins intended for Tai Felton late in the second quarter, which Brown returned 18 yards to the house to extend the 49ers' lead to 28-10. It was his first interception of 2026 and sixth of his career, and Brown is up to 55 tackles (31 solo) and four pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.

The four-time First-Team All-Pro linebacker has double-digit tackles in five of 10 games this season and is up to 96 tackles (42 solo), including 0.5 sacks, five forced fumbles, four pass breakups and a fumble recovery on 96 percent of the Niners' defensive snaps.

Cowing saw limited action in the win, playing just six snaps on offense and two on special teams. The 25-year-old hasn't been targeted across the last two games and should continue to serve a depth role with Mike Evans now healthy.

James went without a touch on offense for the majority of the game, but he was able to turn the team's final two carries of the game into seven yards late in the fourth quarter. The running back was on the field for five offensive plays, and he'll remain the team's No. 3 option behind Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black in Week 12 against the Seahawks.

Juszczyk was able to reel in his first two passes since Week 7, notching his fourth multi-catch performance of the year. The fullback has now caught 10 of 13 targets for 89 yards and two touchdowns while also adding a four-yard rush over nine contests to open the 2026 season.

It was the veteran kicker's third game this season that he didn't attempt a field goal, but he's now gone three straight games with exactly five extra points. Pineiro now leads the league in both point-after attempts (40) and makes (36), but he's attempted just 11 field goals in a highly efficient San Francisco offense. The lack of field goals certainly keeps him from being a top fantasy kicker.

Sunday marked Allen's first time working with Mike Evans, the 49ers' top wide receiver, and the latter dominated the attention of QB Brock Purdy, posting a 6-109-1 line on seven targets in his first game action since Week 6. If Evans' Achilles issue flares up at any point, Allen may be thrust into WR1 duties, which could yield more consistent results as he becomes more acclimated to head coach Kyle Shanahan's offense. For now, though, Allen will play a distant second to Evans for as long as the latter is healthy and available.

The Seahawks listed Smith-Njigba as limited on the first two Week 12 injury reports due to an ankle issue, but he'll play through it in Sunday's NFC West showdown. In the first matchup with the 49ers back in Week 5, he hauled in five of eight targets for 102 yards and one touchdown.

Bradford was listed as limited for the second consecutive day as he continues to deal with a knee injury. The 2023 fourth-round pick should continue to serve as the team's backup right guard behind Grey Zabel during Sunday's matchup against the 49ers.

Cross is seemingly healthy again after having missed the team's last three games due to an ankle injury. The 2022 first-round pick should resume his role as Seattle's starting left tackle during Sunday's matchup against the 49ers.

Lock has been working through an elbow issue to his throwing arm since late October, which has limited his participation in the first two practices of Week 12 prep. He started in each of the Seahawks' two games prior to the Week 11 bye, but is expected to revert to backup duties provided Sam Darnold (quadriceps) is cleared to start against the 49ers on Sunday. If Lock isn't available to play against San Francisco, then Jalen Milroe (illness) would be in line to operate as Seattle's QB2 behind Darnold.

It is unclear where Jones picked up his knee injury, but it still appears to be bothering the linebacker after the Seahawks' Week 11 bye. Jones will have Thursday and Friday's practice sessions to upgrade to full participation and avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's divisional contest against the 49ers.

Nelson underwent a minor procedure on his knee in early November and will be sidelined for a second consecutive game. He's had additional time to rest thanks to the Seahawks' Week 11 bye, and Macdonald relayed Wednesday that the team is "hopeful" that Nelson will be cleared to return for Week 13 against the Cowboys on Monday, Dec. 7. Greg Zabel will likely start at left guard in Nelson's absence.

Per John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site, head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters Wednesday that Lucas is not a candidate for injured reserve but is expected to miss "days to weeks" due to an ankle sprain that he suffered in Week 10 against the Raiders. Josh Jones, Bobby Hart and Chase Lundt are all candidates to start at right tackle for as long as Lucas is sidelined.

questionable

Head coach Mike Macdonald told Brady Henderson of ESPN.com on Wednesday that Darnold will start Sunday at San Francisco if he fares well in practice this week, and a full practice is a good place for the quarterback to kick things off. Darnold has missed the last two contests due to a quad injury and cracked ribs, but only the first concern was mentioned on Wednesday's practice report, indicating his improved level of health.
questionable

Holani was knocked out of the Seahawks' last game in Week 10 at Las Vegas due to a knee injury that eventually was deemed to be an MCL sprain. Per Brady Henderson of ESPN.com, head coach Mike Macdonald said he was uncertain if Holani will require surgery, but the running back will be sidelined for at least four games by virtue of landing on IR. In the meantime, Emanuel Wilson will serve as the team's No. 3 back behind Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price.

Coach Mike MacDonald dialed up the blitz against rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza in his first career start. Two of Witherspoon's four tackles in the Seahawks' win came behind the line of scrimmage off cornerback blitzes against Mendoza. Witherspoon also played all 59 of the team's defensive snaps in the one-score win.

Myers missed a 44-yard field-goal attempt with 7:05 remaining in the game that would have put the Seahawks up 14 points. The kicker is now 16-for-19 on field-goal attempts and 21-for-23 on PATs over 10 regular-season contests in 2026.

It was the third time this season that Kupp recorded only one catch, but the veteran wide receiver made his lone reception count when he found open space on a broken play to connect with Drew Lock for a TD late in the first quarter. It was the third touchdown catch of the season for Kupp, two of which have come over his last three outings. He'll enter the bye with a 23-272-3 line on 35 targets through 10 regular-season games, and the Seahawks' next matchup will take place in Week 12 on the road against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Horton failed to reel in a pass for the first time since Week 7, and his 10 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Seattle behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43), Cooper Kupp (35) and Rashid Shaheed (25). Horton will continue to be an unappealing fantasy option as long as he's buried below the other three wideouts on the depth chart.

Barner has been held below 25 receiving yards in eight of 10 games this season and has more rushing touchdowns (two) than receiving scores (one) during the 2026 campaign. He's the definition of a low-floor, touchdown-or-bust fantasy option headed into the team's bye week.

After missing the previous two games with a knee injury, Shaheed returned against Las Vegas and maintained his role as the WR3 for Seattle. He played 25 of 57 offensive snaps and remained a non-factor in the box score. Shaheed has yet to hit 70 receiving yards in a game this season and has zero touchdowns as a pass catcher. He's off the fantasy radar.

This marks Price's fewest touches in a game since returning from IR in Week 8, and he actually was doubled up in the category by position mate Zach Charbonnet, who turned his 20 rushes into 94 yards. Having said that, Price salvaged his day with a 12-yard TD, the first of his career, on the ground in the third quarter. The breakdown of work between the two may signal what's to come in the Seahawks backfield after the team's Week 11 bye, with Price and company set to face off with the NFC West-leading 49ers on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

Charbonnet was eased in to the mix in Weeks 8 and 9, going from nine touches in the first contest to 17 in the latter. This time around, though, he doubled up fellow RB Jadarian Price in touches (10) and more than did so in terms from yards from scrimmage (44). It may signal that Charbonnet is the Seahawks' clear-cut No. 1 backfield option moving forward, but he won't have a chance to prove as much until after the team's Week 11 bye on Sunday, Nov. 29, at San Francisco.

Reed limped off the field during the first half and was subsequently deemed doubtful to return. Brandon Pili should get a lot more defensive snaps in the likely scenario that Reed is unable to re-enter Sunday's contest.

McMillan hasn't played since Week 3 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, but since he was designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, he was listed as full with knee and calf issues on Thursday's estimated injury report before Friday's downgrade in activity. Ultimately, Saturday's practice report will determine McMillan's chances to return to action Monday against the Panthers.

Parrish is still dealing with the back injury that he suffered in the Week 11 loss to the Lions. The 22-year-old will likely need to be upgraded to a full participant by Saturday's practice to avoid carrying an injury designation into Monday's matchup against the Panthers.

Winfield is still dealing with the ankle injury that he suffered during the Week 9 loss to the Bears. If he is unable to participate at some point over the next two days of practice, the 2020 second-round pick could be in danger of missing a second consecutive game

Trotter popped up on the injury report Thursday, casting doubt on his availability for Monday's matchup against the Panthers. If the rookie second-round pick ends up being unable to play, SirVocea Dennis would likely start at inside linebacker alongside Alex Anzalone.

Rozeboom has been on injured reserve for the Buccaneers' last four games while recovering from a finger injury that he sustained in late October. Tampa Bay's first practice of Week 12 prep is Thursday, so Rozeboom's participation over those three sessions will determine whether he's recovered enough to be activated from IR ahead of Monday's game against the Panthers.

Kieft has played just 11 total snaps on offense over his nine appearances with Tampa Bay this season while Cade Otton, Payne Durham and Bauer Sharp have been prioritized ahead of him at tight end. On the rare occasions he takes the field with the offense, Kieft typically handles a blocking role. He hasn't drawn a target in any game since his second season in the NFL in 2023.

Sharp's 17 percent offensive snap share placed him third among Tampa Bay tight ends, and he trails Cade Otton (97 percent) and Payne Durham (22 percent). The rookie sixth-round pick out of LSU has rarely seen involvement in the passing game over his limited playing time on offense this season, recording a 21-yard reception on two targets over 10 appearances.

Durham's lone contribution in the box score came on the Buccaneers' first play of the day, when he recovered a fumble by quarterback Baker Mayfield. Though he's suited up for each of the Buccaneers' 10 games and has logged double-digit snaps on offense in the past six contests, Durham has recorded just one reception (for five yards) on two targets throughout the season. He's been deployed mainly as a blocking tight end, running routes on just 22 plays on the campaign.

Smith finished second on the team in tackles behind Josiah Trotter, who had 14 (eight solo). Smith has now compiled seven or more tackles across four of his last five appearances and will look to maintain this level of production during the Week 12 matchup against the Panthers.

Simmons played 17 defensive snaps in Sunday's loss but did not appear in the box score. The defensive tackle has now entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to return to full-contact football activities.

Both Morrison and Jacob Parrish (back) were injured in Sunday's loss to Detroit, forcing Tampa Bay to dip into its cornerback depth. Kevin Knowles picked up the extra snaps opposing Zyon McCollum, with Keionte Scott covering the slot.

After making multiple field goals in four straight games leading up to Sunday's game, McLaughlin didn't attempt a field goal for just the second time this season. The veteran kicker remains perfect on 43 kicks this season, going 22-for-22 on field goals and 21-for-21 on PATs. He's a valuable fantasy kicker headed into next Monday night's home date with the Panthers.

Tucker didn't garner any touches on offense for the third straight week as Tampa Bay opted to use Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell exclusively in the backfield. Tucker will continue to have little to no fantasy value as long as both Irving and Gainwell are available for the Buccaneers.

The tight end earned just a 9.1 percent target share and continues to be nearly invisible in the box score despite being an every-down player who runs virtually every pass route for the Bucs. Otton has just one touchdown since Week 11 of the 2024 season and has just one career 100-yard receiving game across 73 regular-season contests. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet who clearly busts far more than he hits.

The veteran wideout ran a team-high 41 routes on Baker Mayfield's 44 dropbacks, but Godwin continues to produce very little with his immense playing time. He's been held under 40 receiving yards in eight straight games and has yet to have a 50-yard receiving game this season. Godwin also has zero touchdowns. He's a low-floor, low-ceiling fantasy option headed into next Monday night's date with the Panthers.

Hurst led the team in targets, and his five catches and 56 receiving yards were new season highs. The wide receiver was able to reach paydirt twice, reeling in a 23-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Baker Mayfield in the second quarter before the pair connected for a four-yard score in the fourth quarter. Hurst has now caught 16 of 32 targets for 224 yards and three touchdowns over 10 contests this season.

Gainwell held his usual complementary role on the ground behind a busy Bucky Irving, yet with the Buccaneers trailing throughout the second half, Gainwell was able to finish second in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the day for Tampa Bay. The veteran back has back-to-back 16-yard efforts on the ground, but Gainwell has a combined 7-103-0 line through the air in that same span heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Panthers on Monday night, Nov. 30.

Egbuka couldn't do much despite tying for the second-most targets on the afternoon for the Buccaneers. The 2025 first-round pick's catch total tied his season low, and he also posted his third sub-20-yard tally of the season. Egbuka has now been held under 50 receiving yards in five consecutive contests heading into a Week 12 Monday night home showdown against the Panthers on Nov. 30.

Mayfield fought through foot and thumb injuries to take the field in a critical game for the 3-6 Buccaneers, but he wasn't able to keep pace with Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs. Mayfield did throw multiple touchdown passes for the first time this season, hitting rookie Ted Hurst for scoring strikes of 23 and four yards. Mayfield's rushing yardage total was also a new season high, and he'll next take aim at the Panthers' beatable secondary in a Week 12 divisional home matchup on Monday night, Nov. 30.

Franklin-Myers' practice reps were limited Wednesday due to a lingering back issue, but his full session Thursday puts the veteran defensive lineman on track to play in Sunday's AFC South tilt against the Jaguars. Franklin-Myers is off to a disappointing start to his Titans tenure, with the 2018 fourth-rounder accumulating 18 tackles (seven solo), including 1.5 sacks, and one pass defense through 10 regular-season games.

Adams has recovered from the illness that sidelined him for the Titans' Week 11 loss to the Cowboys. The safety has already returned to full practice participation and should be all set to continue stringing together prep sessions in anticipation of Sunday's game against the Jaguars.

Granson displayed some pass-catching ability in his first five seasons in the league between stops with the Colts and Eagles, but the Titans have deployed him almost exclusively on special teams in 2026. He's been active for just four of the team's first 10 contests and has drawn just one target while playing three total snaps on offense.

The third-year tight end out of Temple is a core contributor on special teams but has been an afterthought on offense throughout the season. Martin-Robinson hasn't played double-digit snaps on offense in any of his nine appearances and has yet to draw a target.

Winston was able to register at least seven stops for the sixth time this season while playing every defensive snap in Week 11. The safety has now compiled 63 total tackles (35 solo), a forced fumble and a fumble recovery over eight contests so far this season.

Gray finished second on the Titans in tackles behind Joshua Williams (11) in a game that saw Tennessee's defense yield six consecutive touchdown drives to Dallas. Gray has recorded eight stops in back-to-back outings and is up to 54 tackles (30 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and two pass defenses (including one interception).

The Titans' defense failed to put up much of a fight against the Cowboys, who scored touchdowns on each of their first six offensive drives. Williams led Tennessee with a career-high 11 stops, and it was the first time he reached double-digits tackles in a game since entering the league as a fourth-round selection of the Chiefs in the 2022 NFL Draft. He's up to 33 tackles (22 solo) and two pass defenses across five regular-season games.

Starting corner Cor'Dale Flott suffered a neck injury during Sunday's game at Dallas, which could be part of the reason the Titans are looking to add depth in their secondary. Over two games with the Panthers this season, Thornton recorded eight tackles (six solo) and an interception.
Bellinger played 26 offensive snaps and five special-teams snaps in the contest. The tight end capitalized on his sole target but was primarily utilized as a blocker in the blowout loss.

Even with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) out, Restrepo played as the Titans' WR5 against Dallas, as his 17 offensive snaps trailed all four of Carnell Tate (61), Chimere Dike (53), Elic Ayomanor (36) and Calvin Ridley (26). Restrepo played 11 of his 13 snaps in the slot, where Robinson operated prior to his injury, but it was actually Dike and Daniel Bellinger who saw the biggest boosts in slot rate with Robinson out.

With Tyjae Spears (knee) back on the shelf and sent to injured reserve over the weekend, Carter played 14 of 68 offensive snaps behind Tony Pollard in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys. Carter ended up carrying the ball four times for nine yards and caught his lone target for two yards. He should remain Pollard's backup for at least the next three games while Spears is out, unless the Titans have a change of heart and want to start getting rookie Nicholas Singleton some playing time.

Ayomanor logged season highs with five catches, 10 targets and 79 yards against Jacksonville in Week 10, but he reverted back closer to his usual numbers versus the Cowboys. The second-year wideout did rank third on the team in receptions and receiving yards, and his 37 offensive snaps also were third behind Carnell Tate (62) and Chimere Dike (54). Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) is out for the remainder of the season, but Ayomanor may be hard-pressed to put up reliable fantasy production as the third pass-catching option, at best, for one of the league's least prolific air attacks.

The veteran kicker made field goals from 38, 48 and 28 yards in the first half and is in the midst of a career-best season. He's now 18-for-19 on field-goal tries and has made all 17 PATs through 10 games. Kicking in one of the lower-scoring offenses in the league, it still doesn't translate to much fantasy appeal for Slye ahead of next Sunday's road date with the Jaguars.

The tight end has yet to catch a touchdown this season and was unable to get anything going against arguably the league's worst defense Sunday. Helm has been held below 30 receiving yards in nine of 10 games this season. He's nothing more than a low-end TE2 in fantasy.

Dike was able to reel in multiple passes for the third straight game, and his six snags set a new season high for the second-year pro. The 24-year-old paced the team in targets Sunday, narrowly edging out fellow wide receivers Calvin Ridley (six) and Carnell Tate (five). Dike will have a chance to continue carving out a more substantial role for himself on offense moving forward with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) sidelined for the rest of the 2026 campaign.

Ridley reeled in multiple passes in a contest for the first time since Week 5, and his 12-yard touchdown connection with Cam Ward in the fourth quarter was the wideout's first score of the year. Ridley trailed only fellow wide receiver Chimere Dike (seven) in targets, and Ridley could continue to see added opportunities moving forward with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) sidelined for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

Ward's final line belies his struggles somewhat, as a Cowboys defense that made a defensive playcaller switch brought him down for five sacks and forced a lost fumble on one of them at Dallas' 20-yard line. Ward did manage to connect with Carnell Tate (59 yards) and Calvin Ridley (12 yards) for his pair of TD passes, the first coming when the rookie wideout alertly got up after not being touched and the second on a broken play where Ward threw across the field after buying several extra seconds with his legs. Ward also had a one-yard touchdown run in the third quarter, and despite Tennessee's team-level misery, the second-year signal-caller has thrown for at least 231 yards and two touchdowns in three consecutive games heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Jaguars next Sunday.

Tate had a fairly non-descript day overall despite the Titans' 30-point output, but he rewarded fantasy managers with a 59-yard catch-and run touchdown in the third quarter on which he alertly got up and ran down the left sideline after Cowboys defenders failed to touch him while he was down. The rookie fourth overall pick was making his return from a two-game absence due to a shoulder injury, and the score served as Tate's second of his career, both which have come in his last three games. Tate has at least 58 receiving yards in five of the last six contests, including in three straight, heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Jaguars next Sunday.

Burks opened Week 12 prep with back-to-back limited listings due to a lingering foot injury, but a full practice Friday has him in the clear ahead of the weekend. In three appearances since Week 8 while playing with the issue, he's combined for a 7-138-0 line on 11 targets during that span.
out

Diggs had an excused absence Wednesday but avoided the injury report entirely one day later, setting him up to continue to serve as Washington's clear-cut No. 1 wide receiver. Since Terry McLaurin was lost for the season due to a torn patellar tendon that he suffered in Week 6 at San Francisco, Diggs has compiled a 16-217-2 line on 27 targets over the last four games.

Bates went without a target for the fourth straight game. The 29-year-old's 21 offensive snaps ranked third at tight end behind Chig Okonkwo (49) and Ben Sinnott (24), and Bates should continue to have no fantasy value in Week 12 versus the Cardinals.

Chig Okonkwo was the Commanders' only tight end who produced offensively Monday, with the fifth-year pro catching four of five passes for 66 yards. Sinnott has been targeted zero times in seven of 10 regular-season games, with his lone productive outing being Week 10 against the Giants, when he brought in all four of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown. He brings very little fantasy appeal heading into Washington's Week 12 road tilt against Arizona on Sunday.

Jefferson could not hold onto a deep pass from Jayden Daniels early in the fourth quarter, and that catch would have set up the Commanders in the red zone. Jefferson has seen only one pass across his two outings since putting together a 5-58-1 receiving line on seven targets against the Rams in Week 9. Jefferson is firmly entrenched as the Commanders' WR4 behind Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams and Treylon Burks heading into Week 12 against the Cardinals on Sunday.

Stevens had himself a career night in Week 11. The kicker made all five field goals in the second half, converting attempts from 36, 40, 25 and 41 yards before nailing a 26-yard game winner as time expired in regulation. Stevens has now gone 22-for-25 on field-goal tries, including 4-for-7 from 50-plus yards, while making 16 of 19 extra-point attempts over the first 10 games of his rookie campaign.

Jacory Croskey-Merritt returned from a four-game absence due to a groin injury and finished Monday's game with 13 carries for 54 yards. Despite his return, Ekeler ended up with the second-most carries on the Commanders while Rachaad White -- who led Washington's backfield in Croskey-Merritt's absence -- didn't get a single touch on offense. It appears as though Ekeler is the preferred change-of-pace back in Washington's offense heading into Week 12 against Arizona.

With Jacory Croskey-Merritt back from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, White saw a season-low 15 snaps on offense, and the latter's lone carry early in the fourth quarter was nullified by a defensive offside penalty. Croskey-Merritt and Austin Ekeler were responsible for 20 of the Commanders' 26 rushing attempts Monday, and it looks like the return of the former has squeezed White out of the offensive gameplan. The Commanders will hit the road for each of their next two games, starting with Sunday against the Cardinals.

Okonkwo contributed his game-long 32-yard grab on his first catch of the night, and the veteran tight end went on to finish second in receiving yards for the Commanders. He also contributed a key 13-yard grab on Washington's penultimate drive that culminated in a key field goal, and in all, three of his four receptions resulted in first downs. Okonkwo has at least four catches in three straight games but still is seeking his first touchdown of the season heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

The rookie third-round pick managed new career highs across all three components of his receiving line, which also all served as team-best totals Monday. Williams' last two catches of the night were his most critical, as he recorded 22- and 42-yard grabs on Washington's final drive to position Drew Stevens for a game-winning 26-yard field goal. Williams hadn't topped 54 receiving yards in any game after a 64-yard effort in his pro debut in Week 1, but Monday night's breakout could serve as a launchpad to a strong stretch run as the Commanders make a playoff push.

Making his return from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, Croskey-Merritt outpaced Austin Ekeler, the only other Commanders back to log a carry, by six rush attempts. The second-year pro also recorded his third rushing touchdown of the season on a one-yard run with 12 seconds remaining in the first half. Croskey-Merritt averaged over 4.0 yards per carry for the second straight game after failing to eclipse that mark in each of the first four games of the season, and he should be in store for an even busier day in a favorable Week 12 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

Daniels looked like he was on his way to a middling night during a first half in which he led the Commanders to just seven points, but the 2024 first-round pick flipped a switch in the second half, particularly in the fourth quarter. Daniels led field-goal drives of 13, 11 and five plays that netted a total of 193 yards during the final period, the last one featuring strikes of 22 and 42 yards to Antonio Williams to position Drew Stevens for a game-winning field goal. Daniels finished with his second-highest passing yardage total of the season, and he also mustered his seventh interception-free effort of the campaign. Having helped Washington to a critical victory, he'll look to carry the momentum over into a favorable Week 12 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.
Patrick has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol in time for Monday night's contest. Patrick will step back into his starting center role against an improved Bengals defensive line.

Martin's practice reps were limited both Thursday and Friday due to a shoulder issue, but his full session Saturday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Monday night's game. Martin could see an uptick in defensive snaps if defensive back Amik Robertson (ankle) is not cleared to play against Cincinnati.

Tunsil underwent surgery in August to repair a torn triceps. The left tackle continues to recover, but he likely will not suit up for the Commanders in 2026 unless the team makes a playoff run. Even then, it remains unclear whether Tunsil would be able to return at all before the 2027 season.

Yankoff sat out the Commanders' contest against the Giants in Week 10 because of a knee injury, but it now looks like he's put it behind him. He figures to resume a depth role at tight end in Week 11 against the Bengals.

Though he's been active for five straight games while the Commanders' receiving depth has taken hits due to season-ending injuries to Terry McLaurin (knee) and Jaylin Lane (ankle), McCaffrey has yet to carve out much of a role on offense. He took the field for a season-high 14 of the Commanders' 69 offensive plays in Week 10 but went without a target. McCaffrey is likely to continue to provide his greatest impact on special teams, where he appears to have settled in as the Commanders' top return man on both kickoffs and punts.

Reaves finished Thursday's game second on the Commanders in tackles behind rookie first-round linebacker Sonny Styles (13), and the former jumped on a loose ball caused by Frankie Luvu in the third quarter that stopped the Giants' red zone drive. Reaves has logged at least five stops in each of the first nine games of the regular season, and the veteran safety is up to 62 tackles (35 solo), four pass defenses and one fumble recovery on the year.

Cross was one of three Commanders players who played all 65 defensive snaps during Thursday's win. He's posted at least six stops in each of his last three outings, and over that span, he has accumulated 23 tackles (12 solo), three pass defenses (including one interception) and one fumble recovery.
